### Execution approval gate

Committing and reviewing this plan completes planning only. It does not authorize Task 1A. In one trusted Codex task transcript, the plan owner first emits exactly one assistant announcement whose entire normalized body is `Wave 0A plan committed planCommit=C planBlob=O planSha256=S`; no prefix, suffix, second line, or duplicate occurrence is allowed. A later distinct assistant prompt in that same thread has the entire normalized body obtained by substituting the same three lowercase values into `WAVE0A-EXACT-LEASE-MERGE-V1 を承認 planCommit=<40-hex> planBlob=<40-hex> planSha256=<64-hex>`, then yields. Only a still later distinct user message in that thread, whose entire normalized body equals that prompt literal, unlocks implementation. The captured observations have closed roles `assistant_announcement -> assistant_prompt -> user_approval`, one exact `threadId`, and strictly increasing ordinals and observation times; an assistant echo of the approval literal, a user-authored announcement or prompt, a cross-thread message, or an untrusted copied transcript is never approval. This first instruction has `purpose:'implement_committed_wave0a_plan_and_exact_lease_addendum'` and `mutationAuthority:false`: it permits an isolated implementation worktree, source/test/document edits, local read-only verification, local candidate commits, and construction/review of later authority and campaign requests, but it does not permit a live campaign root, control-authority provisioning, disposable-repository mutation, remote ref, PR, workflow dispatch, main update, or cleanup mutation. Its local edit authority is limited to the Wave 0A files enumerated by this detailed plan; it authorizes no Wave 0B ledger/source file, Workflow B/C product capability, Processing capability, conditional R3-R5 work, or downstream detailed plan implementation. The primary agent manually checks the trusted transcript ordering and captures all three message observations plus the exact plan identity once with create-new semantics at `C:\Users\stell\source\archives\bob_builtin_analyze\2026-08-23-feature-integration-approval\wave0a-exact-lease-approval-instruction.json`. The parent is a new non-reparse directory outside every repository/campaign; the closed file is synced, reopened no-follow, identity-hashed, and retained. The producer refuses a plan identity not equal to the committed path, any non-standalone message, any wrong role/thread/order, and approval text whose three embedded identities do not equal that plan. It never infers authority from earlier `承認`, backdates, overwrites, or commits the instruction into the repository. Until this manual gate is satisfied and the captured containing-plan identity re-verifies, status is `BLOCKED_PENDING_POST_PLAN_APPROVAL`; Task 1A does not begin.

### Campaign execution approval gate

After implementation/local gates/independent review fix candidate `B/H/tree`, Task 6I provisions the request-hash-approved final-`H` authority and Task 6H completes lifecycle acceptance through it. Only then may the reviewed producer write canonical `Wave0aCampaignExecutionApprovalRequest` v2 bytes. The request binds branch/local identities, Program/operation contract, 15-operation roster, cumulative DAG digest, complete 9-key authority, lifecycle approval and acceptance `FileIdentity`, acceptance-derived `lifecycleExpiresAt`, attempt/root, one `attemptStartBefore`, and one campaign-start form. `lifecycleExpiresAt` must byte-equal the held lifecycle request/approval/acceptance expiry and `attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`; a generic campaign `expiresAt` remains unknown. New mode binds absent root; existing mode binds root/current head and immediate failed/quarantined predecessor. The separate three-message campaign request-hash approval remains unchanged. Pre-admission `BeginResult` binds immutable template/nonce, including both deadlines, without claiming `attempt_started`. Native admission reopens and holds lifecycle request/approval/claim journal/acceptance plus campaign request/approval, verifies terminal-seal absence and every identity, samples durable `recordedAt`, finalizes/syncs all dependent bytes, performs the last identity/inequality checks, then samples ephemeral `commitFenceNow` and requires `approvedAt <= recordedAt <= commitFenceNow < attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`. The native publish is the immediately following no-yield statement. Root-absent recovery resamples and cannot late-admit; installed-root same-attempt recovery uses durable committed bytes and does not recheck wall clock. Any request/hash/authority/lifecycle/journal/seal/expiry/root/predecessor drift or reused attempt invalidates approval. This campaign approval alone authorizes the bound Wave 0A campaign; planning, provisioning, lifecycle, quarantine, controlled-stop, Wave 0B, and product-source authorities remain distinct.

### Fixed-SHA design closure

The following closure is normative for every later task and test in this plan. Implementation must remove the superseded spellings and branches listed here rather than preserve aliases. Where an older explanatory paragraph or code block below still describes a narrower recovery window, a staging-owned release attestation, direct multi-exit native invocation, split root-planning/publication commands, or a contradictory partial worktree removal, this section and the corresponding Task 6A/6B/6E/6F/6G/8A edits are the closed contract.

1. **All-mutation precheckpoint recovery.** Every one of the 15 operation instances can be discovered after durable request/intent and before a campaign checkpoint as exactly one `operation_precheckpoint` window. The window binds the source handoff/event/index head, request, intent, exact operation prefix, execution-plan SHA, program-state SHA, topology, attachments, claim/proof/result ownership, and one of four programs: ordinary `observe_only_no_spawn`, generated-cleanup suffix, root-fast-forward suffix, or worktree-removal suffix. Historical `recover` authenticates and publishes validation/preservation/failure/`mutation_reconciliation_required` checkpoint plus an intent-only recovered handoff, then stops; it never executes business mutation. A fresh generation alone calls `reconcile-existing`. Ordinary operations never respawn; a durable result is reconciled; only the three journaled programs may execute the exact missing same-intent suffix. A second unresolved intent, non-next operation, changed source/event/index/intent/program state, or action/program crossing is an integrity stop.
2. **Journaled worktree removal.** Worktree removal uses immutable delete ordinals and a bounded progress journal, not an all-or-nothing contradiction rule. Missing nodes must be exactly a contiguous authorized prefix `1..P`; remaining nodes, Git registration, release activation, process/CWD chain, target/admin parents, and every no-follow identity must still match. The helper preopens the remaining suffix, disposes only `P+1..N`, publishes progress at each 1,024-entry boundary and at the final boundary, and emits the canonical result only at `P=N`. A mid-chunk crash is resumed from the exact observed prefix without repeating a disposition; a crash after a boundary and before publication creates a `reconciled_after_crash` progress record. Gap, replacement, reparse, unexpected child, registration/CWD/release drift, or progress/filesystem disagreement is contradictory. Maximum is 16 progress records and `1 claim + 16 progress + 1 result = 18` reserved slots.
3. **Neutral release supervisor.** The authority-installed `wave0a-stage-minus-one.ps1` has a public `-Supervise` role and private controller-child role in addition to `-DefineOnly`. The supervisor starts in the credential-authority root, owns the sole non-inheritable kill-on-close Job handle, creates outer/host/operator suspended, assigns all three to one controller generation before resume, and writes `held/active-controller-tree.json` before operator resume. The active-tree record binds supervisor session/generation plus exact outer/host/operator PID, creation time, and CWD identities. Controller exit `42` plus the fixed `StageStopResult` is the only handoff signal; `root_handoff_ready` is consumed inside that same supervisor. Controller crash starts an authenticated `recover` generation; only typed non-root stop/final outcomes leave the supervisor.
4. **Durable root release quartet.** Each release ordinal under the authority-owned `controllerReleaseRoot` consists of create-new `request.json`, companion `result.txt`, `envelope.json`, and `activation.json`. The campaign publisher writes request/result/envelope; the neutral supervisor creates the next outer suspended, proves the prior three-process tree exited and the new root CWD is correct, durable-writes activation, and only then resumes the new controller. `ControllerReleaseBootstrapContext` contains exactly `{activation,companionResult,envelope,request}` identities. Nothing in predecessor staging is release authority. Reentry reopens the quartet; after an activated generation fails, historical recovery allocates the next release ordinal and never reuses an activation.
5. **One root publication transaction.** Production exposes only `publish-root-handoff --root ABS --attempt-id ID --source-verified-handoff ABS --expected-state MAIN_ONLY|MERGED --expected-profile ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED|POST_MERGE_FAILURE_ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED --operation-receipt ABS --active-controller-tree ABS AUTHORITY_ARGS --output NEW_STAGING_RESULT`. One supervised `campaign_publisher` claim computes the plan, create-new writes the durable request first, commits/adopts the byte-identical campaign handoff/index transaction, then writes durable companion result and envelope and finally the staging publication result. `CampaignPublisherOperation` and lock binding use internal operation literal `create_root_handoff`. Superseded split root-planning/root-creation commands and every separate PowerShell release-request writer are absent.
6. **Root bootstrap and remove request.** `rehydrate` has three exclusive forms: generic Handoff, generic HandoffResult, or root quartet `--controller-release-envelope/--controller-release-request/--controller-release-companion-result/--controller-release-activation`; the root form forbids generic result. `recover` additionally accepts a root envelope and derives/revalidates its request/result/activation. Host request/attestation and every manifest bind the supervisor session and active-tree identity. `mutation-request` accepts `--controller-release-bootstrap-result ABS` if and only if `operationInstanceId='remove-feature-worktree'` in either mode, and forbids it for every other operation/mode union branch. The request keeps immutable pre-intent active-tree/release proof; an actual helper PID is recorded only in the post-spawn claim. Every remove caller passes the bootstrap-result path, never an in-memory context object.
7. **Typed native exits and authority argv.** Every multi-exit CLI goes through `Invoke-Wave0aNativeMultiExit`; direct invocation is a source-test failure. The mutation runner recognizes `0/20/21/22/73/74/75`. Local gate uses `0/1`; mergeability, lifecycle, exact-CI and discovery use their declared `0/20/21/1` subsets; settlement uses `0/20/21/1`. `$externalToolArgv` replaces exactly one post-Stage-0 `AUTHORITY_ARGS` slot, while `$preCampaignAuthorityArgv` replaces exactly one Task-6I-approval-derived `PRECAMPAIGN_AUTHORITY_ARGS` slot; neither may cross, coexist in one mode, or be repositioned by similarly named output flags, and process-free modes receive neither tuple. The tuple is not executable-code authority: every pre-campaign launch uses the authenticated Node and requires the Task 6E supervisor to acquire/authenticate every installed final-`H` bundle member before interpreter creation and retain all write/delete-denying handles through child exit and stream settlement; partial acquisition or any pre-spawn lease failure means zero spawn. After creation, a detected lifetime violation fences further spawns, kills and settles the existing child, rejects its output, and only then releases the handles. Every post-Stage-0 Git observation—including clean-status—uses the authenticated bounded fixed-argv wrapper rather than direct `& $gitExecutable`. Task 6D `plan-removal` is process-bearing because it launches the authority-bound native `inspect-path` helper: `--native-helper` remains a mode-specific business input outside the tuple, and the one contiguous `$externalToolArgv` expansion remains immediately before `--output`.
8. **PR settlement stops.** `settle-integrated-pr` always writes verified observation then settlement for semantic exits: `0=settled_merged`, `20=poll_exhausted`, `21=closed_unmerged`; `1` is producer/validation failure and writes neither complete output. Timeout is exactly 120 OPEN observations; CLOSED is the first terminal CLOSED after zero or more OPEN; MERGED is the sole terminal MERGED. Exit 20/21 is campaign-owned as `integration-settlement`, then produces `pr_settlement_failed` with `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_TIMEOUT` or `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED`, a verified checkpoint/handoff, and phase exit 42. It performs no fetch/event/cleanup. `CONTROLLED_POST_INTEGRATION_STOP` can only reverify and reissue that stop until a separate captured approval selects a new campaign disposition.
9. **Post-integration main drift.** If the exact two-ref integration was applied at `M` but live main is later authenticated as `K`, the only accepted drift is `K != B`, `K != M`, `M` ancestor of `K`, feature ref absent, remote heads main-only, and the named PR identity consistent with its terminal/OPEN state. This produces no applied integration receipt; it records the typed `post_integration_main_drift` reconciliation plus `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT`, exact `K/M/B`, preparation parents/tree, a `topology_drift` checkpoint/handoff, and phase exit 42. Settlement, fetch, dispatch, cleanup, retry push, reset, and force-push are forbidden. The controlled stop can only be reissued until a separately captured terminal/rebaseline decision.
10. **Capacity and literal gates.** The charge generator includes reconciliation capacity from attempt start for all still-unconsumed operations. Worktree progress adds at most 48 operation-tree files and 65,536 progress bytes, but no attempt/handoff attachment. Existing limits (`MAX_RECOVERY_CHECKPOINTS=32`, `MAX_HANDOFFS=56`, operation slot cap 100, claim/proof cap 128, attempt cap 140, evidence cap 512 MiB) may remain only after exact `N-1/N/N+1` positive-headroom tests. The schema test fixes `KnownAttachmentSchema/AttachmentByteCapBySchema/AttachmentPayload=42/42/42`, operations `15/15/15`, twelve Stage 0 manifest rows, the root member counts defined by the final manifest below, 40 attestation keys, five READY refs, sixteen fixture-manifest attachments, and a four-key controller-release context.

### Normative downstream master roadmap

このsectionはWave 0A後の任意メモではなく、機能取捨選択とmain逐次統合のmandatory program planである。以下のboundary、採否、順序、gate、stop、closureはこのplanのnormative scopeに含まれる。一方、将来のexact mainに依存するfile path、test名、CLI、campaign schemaを先書きしないため、詳細なcode mutation手順は各boundary直前の別planで固定する。その詳細plan自身もrepository mutationであるため、plan作成前の専用request-hash承認と、commit済みplanを固定する実装前の別request-hash承認を混同しない。したがって、現在のplanはProgram全体を計画するが、最初の`WAVE0A-EXACT-LEASE-MERGE-V1`承認によって直ちに実装できるのはWave 0Aのlocal candidateまでだけである。Wave 0B以降のplan／source／product／evidence mutation、remote ref、PR、workflow dispatch、merge、cleanupは一切その承認へ相乗りしない。

#### Wave 0B source universe and selection ledger

The two admission arms are static policy in Wave 0A only, not an executable selector or new CLI. Wave 0B concretizes both arms in all three downstream protocol families. Optional closure's first admission binds the complete FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL terminal VERIFIED identity, the exact fixed product main/tree/payload, and the successful four-phase external attestation; revision, recovery, or disposition/restart preserves that same initial admission subject and may not substitute a different attestation or select a second closure. The no-prior-closure check applies to first admission; a resume must instead authenticate the sole matching prior subject. Final attestation content is unavailable until FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL is VERIFIED, so the optional arm fails closed until then.

Wave 0Bはproduct capabilityを実装しない。最初のdownstream PRは、5 remaining carrier ranges、Workflow P4-R6の旧head、Contribution range、Processing prerequisite/T13-T18の旧head、closed PR mapping、およびimmutable archive manifest/bundle/patchを入力に、次をmainへ統合する。

- `tools/main-consolidation/feature-selection-source-universe.json`: exact 40桁from/to SHA、sorted commit/path/source-test manifestsと各SHA-256、old PR、candidate capability、symbol/contract/test単位の`sourceItemId`、explicit remainderを決定的に生成する。
- `docs/release-evidence/feature-selection-ledger-2026-08-23.json`: source universe digest、baseline/topology/archive identities、capability、discriminated `sourceOrigin`、一つのdisposition、rationale、`hardDependsOn`、`sequenceAfter`、GO/approval requirement、最大activation、target surface、invariant、omission、acceptance gateを固定する。
- `docs/release-evidence/feature-selection-ledger-2026-08-23.md`: JSONからbyte-deterministicに生成し、手編集またはJSONとのdriftを拒否する。
- schema/policy/generator/testsと外部append-only execution/status projection contract。future implementation head、merge SHA、run/UAT resultをstatic ledgerへplaceholder、`null`、予測値で書かない。
- `PROGRAM-SLICE-PLAN-AUTHORING-V1`、`PROGRAM-SLICE-IMPLEMENTATION-V1`、`PROGRAM-SLICE-WORKSPACE-DISPOSITION-V1`: closed schema、canonical request/approval/result producer、validator、trusted-transcript capture、negative/replay/recovery fixtureをWave 0Bの同じsliceで統合する。P4以降はこのmain上の実装だけを使い、caller-supplied slice/predecessor/workspace/dispositionを受け付けない。

全commit/path/test/source itemはexact一つのsource trancheとprimary owner capabilityまたはexplicit remainderへ割り当てる。共有利用は非所有`consumedBy`として記録し、missing、duplicate primary owner、未承認overlap、未分類remainderを一件でも残した状態をWave 0B successにしない。Wave 0B independent reviewは機械的coverageだけでなく、mixed-purpose commit、T17/T18 subset、Contribution rangeのsemantic boundaryを確認する。

Static dispositionは次の四つだけであり、criteriaを満たす一つを各capabilityまたはexplicit remainder recordへ設定する。各source item自身はexact一つのprimary owner capability/remainderへ割り当てられ、そのownerのdispositionとrationaleから追跡できるようにし、source item単位の別dispositionで二重判断を作らない。

| Disposition | Selection criteria | Program action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `selected` | current mainに未所有のrequired behaviorで、exact source/provenance、依存閉包、owned surface、preserved invariant、RED/acceptance evidence、Linux/Windows要件を閉じられ、duplicate authorityや暗黙のpublic API/settings/schema/version変更を作らない | mandatory sequenceで一つずつ再実装・検証・統合する |
| `conditional` | valueはあるが、別spec/security/Windows実機/activationなど明示GO evidenceと別approvalが未充足 | mandatory program後までsourceを統合せず、後述の別campaignだけがGOできる |
| `rejected_current_snapshot` | archive snapshotに安全性/complete recovery/現行contract適合の不足があり、そのbytesを現在の製品へ入れない | archive evidenceだけ保持し、将来は新ID/spec/reviewが必要 |
| `superseded` | current mainまたは別selected sliceが同等以上の唯一のauthorityを持つ | duplicate implementation/test/gateを移植せず、remainder rationaleを固定する |

Mandatory `selected` setは`WF2-P4-COMPILER`、`WF2-P5-PLANSTORE`、`WF2-P6-ENTRYPOINT`（shadow only）、`WF2-P7-MANIFEST`、`WF2-R1-PROVENANCE`、`WF2-R2-INVOKE`（product runtime unreachable）、`REG-BRIDGE-OWNER-VERSION-LIFECYCLE`、`REG-BRIDGE-DISCOVERY-EVIDENCE`、`PROC-T13-LEDGER`、`PROC-T14-BOUNDED-DOC`、`PROC-T15-AGGREGATE`、`PROC-T16-INPUT-PROCESS`、`PROC-T17-DEADLINE`、`PROC-T17-PATH`、`PROC-T18-REPORT`、`PROC-T18-CCR-HANDOFF`、`PROC-T18-BZR-HANDOFF`で固定する。`WF2-R3-WINDOWS-ADAPTER`、`WF2-R3-ARTIFACT-TX`、`WF2-R4-EXECUTOR`、`WF2-R5-BOB`は`conditional`、`WF2-R6-ARCHIVED`は`rejected_current_snapshot`、`REG-P1-PREREQUISITE-REMAINDER`、旧compiler/duplicate registry/旧Bazaar OOXML・GUI分割/旧Workflow A複製などはreviewed source-item単位の`superseded`とする。`not_applicable`はstatic dispositionではなく、mandatory `FINAL-VALIDATION`後に別planが定義するevidence-bearing conditional selectorのpossible dynamic outcomeにすぎず、Wave 0Bで未分類や未承認を隠す値として使用しない。

この17件の`selected` capabilityはmandatory downstream mutation catalog全体ではない。`programAtomicSlices`はこれらにWave 0B selection/protocol slice、Gate R composite slice、`FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL`を加えたexact 20 rowsである。Gate PはP7後のrepository-non-mutating boundary completion observationなので21番目のmutation sliceには数えない。Wave 0Aはこのdownstream 20-row catalogのimmediate predecessorでありcatalog自身には含めない。任意の`FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE`は`finalValidationPolicy.closure`由来のcatalog外descriptorであり、mandatory row数を変更しない。

Wave 0Bは上記判断をarchive実体へ照合して確定するgateであり、実体と合わないことを理由にその場で採否を変更しない。Missing source、unexpected dependency、semantic boundary conflict、current-main ownership drift、またはacceptance evidence不足が一つでも見つかれば`WAVE-0B-SELECTION-LEDGER`を停止し、original bytesとinventoryを保全してProgram amendment planと新しいrequest-hash承認を要求する。静的ledgerを実装都合やtest failureに合わせて書き換えない。

#### Mandatory one-at-a-time integration sequence

次のtableは`programAtomicSlices`のexact 20 rowsとその非変更completion observationを人間向けに投影する。`Ordered units`でatomic sliceと列挙した各矢印要素は一つのlatest-main branch、candidate、PR、merge、exact-main verification、main-only cleanup、terminal recordを持ち、そのmandatory catalog rowのimmediate predecessorが`VERIFIED`になるまで次をplanまたは実装しない。Gate P attestationはP7後のrepository-non-mutating boundary observationであり、五つ目のsliceではない。`FINAL-VALIDATION`は最初に`FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL`を通常sliceとして統合し、そのVERIFIED exact mainをfixed product mainとしてaggregate gate、build、UAT、topology auditを順序付きnon-mutating phasesで実行する。Phaseごとのbranch、PR、merge、cleanupは作らず、全phase成功後にrepository内publicationが必要な場合だけ、最大一つの`FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE` docs/evidence-only atomic sliceをpolicy由来のoptional admission armと同じ三段階承認protocolで実行する。

| `PROCESSING-INTEGRITY` | `T18 report -> T18 CCR handoff -> T18 Bazaar handoff` | deterministic complete report、partial rejection、complete-only atomic handoff/rollback |
| `FINAL-VALIDATION` | `FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` mutation slice -> VERIFIED exact mainをproduct mainとしてfreeze -> non-mutating aggregate gates -> fresh three-VSIX build -> same-artifact real-machine UAT -> read-only final topology audit -> optional `FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE`（最大一つ） | control/tooling integrated、external attestationだけ、またはpayload-preserving closure sliceのattestationでall selected capabilities `validated`、remote/local main-only |

Workflow BはP4のsole immutable compiler、P5のprivate per-environment cache/runtime-only lease、P6の共通gatewayとfixed-policy shadow、P7のexplicit collection/catalog manifestを順に追加し、既存v1 validation/registration/`Bob 操作ハブ`/Bob/authoringを維持する。Workflow Cはarchive testを直接active runnerへ混ぜず、inventoryでR1-R6を一意分類し、active manifestへmerge済みR1/R2だけを追加する。R1/R2はprovenance/invocation境界だけを統合し、run-directory、provider dispatch、Bob task、artifact stagingへのpublic/product active pathをstatic reachabilityとruntime spyの両方で0にする。Contribution bridgeはowner/version/lifecycleとdiscovery/evidenceを別sliceにし、legacy compiler、second registry、manual catalogを持ち込まない。

Processingは現行OOXML安全化を置換しない。T14はvalidated snapshot `Buffer`、通常OOXML再圧縮0、missing-both XLSXだけminimal stylesheet、lazy dependency、post-extraction fingerprint、fixed GUI diagnosticを維持してshared budgetへ接続する。T17はdeadlineとpathを別sliceにし、Windows process tree、junction/UNC、日本語/空白/multi-rootとLinux process groupをreal-OS blockerにする。T18はreport、CCR handoff、Bazaar handoffを別sliceにし、report `complete`かつ全reservation finalized以外をatomic replacementへ渡さない。

`FINAL-VALIDATION`はまず通常の`FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` atomic sliceで、opaqueに予約したproduct-payload/UAT-artifact/final-attestation schemas、canonical producers/parsers/validators、external publication/recovery、fixtures、Program-index/status linkageを実装し、exact-head/main gateとmain-only cleanupを経て`VERIFIED`にする。そのexact mainを`productMainSha`、`productTreeSha`、build対象source/lockfileの`productPayloadManifestSha256`として一度freezeし、同じexact product mainのfresh cloneに対してaggregate local/hosted gates、3 VSIX build/hash、same-bytes real-machine UAT、read-only final topology auditをこの順で実行する。これら4つは全てrepository/product-topology non-mutating validation phasesであり、repository branch/worktree/commit、remote ref、PR、merge、campaign、cleanupをphaseごとに作成または変更しない。Build/UATが書けるのはattestationで先に固定したfresh external artifact/profile/evidence rootsだけであり、source cloneとproduct mainはread-only identityとして再検証する。Phase outputはrepository外のhash-linked final attestationへ追記する。Repository内closure publicationが不要なら、そのexternal attestationが`FINAL-VALIDATION`をproduct mainのまま`VERIFIED`にする。必要なら全phase成功後、`finalValidationPolicy.closure`からのみ導出したoptional descriptor、controlのterminal VERIFIED、fixed product main/tree/payloadへ結合した成功phase attestation、先行closure 0件をadmissionで固定して最大一つだけ`FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE`を同じplan-authoring／implementation／campaign protocolへ通し、変更をallowlisted docs/evidence pathsだけに限定し、`productPayloadManifestSha256`と全product payload file identityがproduct mainからexact-head/mainまでbyte-identicalであることを証明する。Evidence-only mergeを理由にproduct UATを循環再実行せず、closure merge SHA、CI、branch deletion、final topologyを同じexternal attestationへ追加する。Product/UAT identityとoptional evidence-publication identityを同じSHAとして扱わない。

Final real-machine UATは、Workflow Bのpackage/lock/plan/manifest決定性、既存v1/Bob/authoring導線とP6 shadow、Workflow C R1/R2のproduct execution reachability 0、実DOCX/XLSX/PDFのRules/Verification/PDF locator/原本bytes不変と上限超過・partial handoff拒否、timeout/cancel後のchild process 0、`bzr --no-aliases`とShift-JIS診断、multi-root/日本語/空白/UNC/junction escape境界、Extension Hostのuncaught/unhandled/CSP/dangling callback 0、`readFiles(...).then is not a function` 0と別failureのdiagnostic retentionを同じartifact identitiesへ結合する。既存`PRA-WIN-001`はbaselineだけに保全して新mainで再実行し、`PRA-WIN-002`〜`008`をこのmandatory Programの暗黙gateへ昇格させない。

#### Common exact-head, review, merge, and stop gates

各PR-bearing atomic slice（必要時の`FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE`を含む）の詳細planは、少なくとも次の順序を削除・並列化せず、current mainでexact command/path/job setを埋める。`FINAL-VALIDATION`のaggregate/build/UAT/topology phasesにはこのPR slice gateを重ねず、直前paragraphのfixed-product-main non-mutating sequenceとexternal attestation gateを適用する。

1. Derived admissionDescriptorとそのarmに必要なevidence、dependency terminal records、base/main/topologyを再検証する。Selected capabilityではarchive/source identityとselection rowを要求する。Optional closureではselected sourceの代わりにfixed product main/tree/payloadと成功phase attestationを要求し、docs/evidence descriptorだけを使用する。`PROGRAM-SLICE-PLAN-AUTHORING-V1`でlatest mainから作成され、`PROGRAM-SLICE-IMPLEMENTATION-V1`が同一identityの継続使用を許可した唯一のworktree/branchを再認証する。ここで二つ目を作らず、旧patch全適用または旧commitの無差別cherry-pickをしない。
2. Derived descriptorのbehavior/invariant/omissionを表すRED testsを先に実在させる。Selected capabilityはselection rowのselected source itemだけをcurrent interfacesへ実装し、optional closureはallowlisted docs/evidence publicationとpayload不変検証だけを行う。unowned path、unrelated dependency/lockfile/generated changeは許可しない。
3. Local gateは`compile -> focused tests -> full tests -> dependency/architecture/source/schema/unused/artifact/audit policy -> package/smoke/metrics as applicable -> git diff --check`の順とし、changed componentおよび全affected consumerを実行する。platform固有mandatory behaviorはUbuntu/Windows両方をrequiredにする。
4. PR campaignはexact `B/H/tree`を固定し、required workflowがPR eventまたは`workflow_dispatch expectedHeadSha=H`で明示的に`H`をcheckoutし、run/job ID、event、head/ref、attempt、required/skipped集合をfail-closedで照合する。synthetic merge ref、latest run、別head run、missing/skipped required jobを成功証拠にしない。
5. Exact-head CI成功後、別task/reviewerがfull `B...H`をreviewし、Critical 0 / Important 0を要求する。Hまたはchanged-path manifestが一byteでも変わればlocal gates、CI、reviewを全て無効化する。
6. Separate live campaign approvalが固定した操作だけで一度mergeし、merge parents/tree/method、PR settlement、branch deletionを検証する。main/base/head drift、lease mismatch、unexpected PR/refは停止し、force/reset/admin bypassで合わせない。
7. Exact merged main `M`で全required workflowをfresh dispatchし、local aggregate/full policy/packageを再確認する。artifact/UAT boundaryは`M`のfresh clean cloneからbuildした同一bytesを使う。
8. Allowlisted generated output、feature branch/worktree/archive refsをbounded cleanupし、`main == origin/main == live remote main == M`、remote/local branchは`main`だけ、open PR 0、registered worktree rootだけ、protected nested clone不変を証明してからそのsliceを`VERIFIED`にする。

いずれかのarchive/source/selection/dependency/main drift、unclassified item、semantic omission、duplicate authority、unexpected path/lockfile、OOXML/GUI/v1 regression、conditional activation、platform片側だけの成功、local/CI/review/package/UAT failure、PR/head/base/merge mismatch、cleanup/topology ambiguityでそのsliceを停止する。失敗に合わせてstatic ledgerを書き換えず、candidate/evidenceを保全し、詳細planが定義したtyped recoveryまたはseparately approved replacement attemptだけを行う。安全にmain-onlyへ戻ったterminal non-successであってもboundary successではなく、次sliceへ進まない。

#### Conditional follow-on and final main-only disposition

`FINAL-VALIDATION`のmandatory UAT、final attestation、main-only auditが`VERIFIED`になる前はR3-R5をplan、branch、実装、activationしない。その後もconditional-selector／activation planは現在のmandatory/optional-closure二arm protocolの対象外であり、別途承認された将来のspec／authority設計を先に要する。その別設計が一つのplan-only workspaceとplan作成権限、committed-plan-bound implementation権限を明示した後だけ、purpose-discriminated GO/NOGO selector、exact Program-index/selection-ledger/main/predecessor identities、freshness、nonce、`maxUses:1`、request-hash approval、evidence-bearing `not_applicable` outcomeを設計・統合できる。現planは新たなselector、CLI、第三armまたはその実装権限を定義しない。GOを得たcapabilityだけを、`WF2-R3-WINDOWS-ADAPTER -> WF2-R3-ARTIFACT-TX -> WF2-R4-EXECUTOR -> WF2-R5-BOB`の順で、それぞれ別のplan-authoring request-hash approval、detailed plan、implementation request-hash approval、candidate、live campaign approval、PR、exact-head/main gates、UAT、main-only cleanupとして直列実行する。R3 Windows adapterはnew-design spec、security review、reparse/junction/mount escape/hard-link substitution/identity drift/no-overwrite/flush/failure-injectionのWindows実機proofがGO前提である。前段mergeだけで後段を自動GOしない。

NOGOまたはGO未取得ならcapabilityはstatic ledgerの`conditional`のまま終了し、それ自体はmandatory program failureではない。Conditional campaignを一つでも実行した場合は、その都度fresh three-VSIX build、affected real-machine UAT、exact-main aggregate gates、final attestation、remote/local main-only auditを再実行する。`WF2-R6-ARCHIVED`はこのgraphへ入れず、current snapshotのbranch/source/testを統合しない。将来のresume/restartは新capability ID、新spec、新selection decision、新request-hash approvalを要する。

Programの最終steady stateは、全mandatory `selected` rowsがexternal/status evidenceで`validated`、全conditional rowsが未統合の`conditional`または別campaignで`validated`、rejected/superseded sourceがmainへ混入せず、remote heads `['main']`、open PR 0、local branch `['main']`、registered worktree root 1、local-only `refs/archive/**` 0、`main == origin/main == live remote main`、protected nested clone byte-identicalである。旧feature branch/worktree/archiveの削除は各identityのreachability/evidence保全を確認したapproved cleanup stepだけで行い、roadmapを理由に一括削除しない。

## File map

The normative implementation dependency order is `1A -> 1B -> 6A -> 1C -> 2 -> 3A -> 3B -> 4A -> 4B -> 5A -> 6E -> 5B -> 6B -> 6C -> 6D -> 6F -> 6G -> 6H -> 6I -> 7 -> 8A -> 8B`. The headings below keep related policy/execution material together, but an implementer must follow this dependency order. Task 6A lands the pure closed schemas, shared producer fixtures, and `CommandObservation` types immediately after the Program authority; later archive/CI/topology/local-gate producers import those fixtures. The reviewed Windows/native bounded primitive exists before Task 5B, Task 6B, Task 6C, Task 6H, or Task 6I uses it. Completing Task 6H here means its repository code/tests/review; live ordering after every Task 1–6H commit and aggregate review is final-`H` control-authority approval/provisioning in 6I, owner supply of one existing disposable repository, read-only eligibility preflight through that authority, lifecycle request/approval/acceptance through 6H, then campaign request/approval; none can be reordered or inferred from another gate. If no eligible owner-provided repository exists, status is `BLOCKED_PENDING_DISPOSABLE_REPOSITORY` and no lifecycle request is created.

Every command block is executed by a checked runbook wrapper under `Set-StrictMode -Version Latest`, `$ErrorActionPreference='Stop'`, and PowerShell 7 `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$true`. A native call with exactly one success exit captures `$LASTEXITCODE` immediately and aborts before the next line on nonzero, signal, timeout, or overflow. Every CLI whose grammar assigns more than one semantic exit must instead use the single tested operator-private `Invoke-Wave0aNativeMultiExit`: in a `try/finally` it temporarily sets `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference=$false`, invokes the exact token argv without a shell, captures one `[int]$LASTEXITCODE` immediately, restores the prior preference, rejects spawn failure without reusing an old exit, validates the caller's closed allowed-exit set, and returns only that typed exit. No multi-exit CLI may be invoked directly. A later test, `git diff --check`, serialization, or commit can never mask an earlier failure. RED steps are the only exception: they declare the exact expected nonzero and fail if the command unexpectedly returns zero or a different failure class. Multi-line snippets below remain separate asserted invocations even where the repeated wrapper call is omitted for readability. After every `git add`, `git diff --cached --name-only` must equal that step's literal staging list, which must be a subset of the task's `Files:` ownership list; before the task's final review, the ordinal union of all step staging lists must equal the complete task ownership list exactly. This permits the explicitly planned split commits in Tasks 6E/6G without permitting an unowned path.

// tools/main-consolidation/wave0aProposalPolicy.mjs
export function buildWave0aEventProposal({ operation, verifiedHandoff, operationInput, attachmentSlots })
export function buildWave0aPullRequestBody({ verifiedHandoff, authenticatedEvidence })
export function buildWave0aRecoveryRecords({ source, failure, preservation, observations }) // source is exactly VerifiedHandoff|HistoricalBootstrapResult

// tools/main-consolidation/boundedNativeProcess.mjs
export async function runBoundedNativeProcess({ executable, argv, cwd, deadline, limits, processAdapter })

// tools/main-consolidation/run-wave0a-mutation.mjs (private controller boundary)
// Not exported by boundedNativeProcess.mjs and never accepted by local-gate callers.
runWave0aSupervisedOperation(request: Wave0aSupervisedOperationRequest): Promise<VerifiedNativeOutput<Wave0aSupervisedOperationResult>>
buildTerminationProofReservation(request: TerminationProofReservationBuildRequest): TerminationProofReservationBuildResult
recoverOperationPublication(request: OperationPublicationRecoveryRequest): Promise<VerifiedNativeOutput<OperationPublicationRecoveryResult>>

// tools/main-consolidation/wave0aMutationPolicy.mjs
export function buildWave0aMutation({ operationId, verifiedHandoff, topology, evidence })
export function assessWave0aMutationResult({ request, intent, processResult, postObservation })
```

Exact-head `assess`はverified campaign-owned run-discovery recordから4 workflowのnumeric run IDを導出し、caller-supplied run IDを受け取らない。run検索・因果選択はread-only discovery adapterだけが行い、before集合、trigger boundary、dispatch nonce/title、after集合のclosed policyを通す。`assessSliceTopology`は`READY`、`LOCAL`、`PR_ACTIVE`、`MERGED`、`POST_MERGE_VERIFIED`、`MAIN_ONLY`、`VERIFIED`と全recovery profileを区別し、mutationを行わず、stable profileではbefore/after observationsが同一でない場合に失敗する。Proposal/mutation builderの`operationInput`/`topology`/`evidence`は後掲のoperation-discriminated closed unionであり、任意keyの`trustedInputs` bagは存在しない。 Run discovery receives the complete closed trigger boundary, recomputes its canonical SHA against `request.triggerBoundarySha256`, and rejects hash-only or crossed boundaries. Exact-CI receives exactly four run API observations keyed by the discovered IDs plus their jobs, and validates repository/workflow/event/head/ref/title/status/conclusion before job linkage. Integrated-PR settlement uses the explicit shared signature above for both initially merged and initially pending fixtures; adapter tests require that exact call shape.

- [ ] **Step 1: Reconfirm the planning boundary before editing**

Run from the isolated worktree with a caller-held absolute Git executable, the canonical absolute repository root, and the no-follow-held post-plan approval instruction. Before the first Git call, reject any inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_COMMON_DIR`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES`, `GIT_NAMESPACE`, or `GIT_CONFIG_*` selector; set the same sanitized config environment later fixed by Task 6E. `Read-ClosedPostPlanApprovalInstruction` is a built-in-only, strict UTF-8/JSON/no-follow verifier for the exact captured v4 instruction described by the execution gate. It accepts no repository code and returns the three approved lowercase identities only after `purpose:'implement_committed_wave0a_plan_and_exact_lease_addendum'`, `mutationAuthority:false`, and the single `trustedTranscript` with `source:'codex_trusted_transcript_v1'`, one bound `threadId`, and exact standalone role-ordered `assistantAnnouncement`, `assistantPrompt`, and later `userApproval` all reverify. An assistant-authored approval echo or any cross-thread observation rejects.

```powershell
$expectedBase = 'c59db06ecb32eb7a57beeb3e932acdd5b4774de5'
$specCommit = '819d6261d52d8dc7037d7fae8b852ad4b6a52e21'
$specPath = 'docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-23-feature-selection-and-sequential-main-integration-design.md'
$planPath = 'docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-23-feature-integration-program-index-and-wave-0a.md'
$approval = Read-ClosedPostPlanApprovalInstruction -LiteralPath $approvalInstructionPath
$planCommit = [string]$approval.planCommit
$approvedPlanBlob = [string]$approval.planBlob
$approvedPlanSha256 = [string]$approval.planSha256
$mergeBaseRaw = & $gitExecutable -C $repositoryRoot merge-base $expectedBase HEAD
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'cannot resolve planning merge base' }
if ($mergeBaseRaw.Trim() -ne $expectedBase) { throw 'planning branch lost the approved base' }
$specBlobRaw = & $gitExecutable -C $repositoryRoot rev-parse "$specCommit`:$specPath"
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'cannot resolve approved spec blob' }
if ($specBlobRaw.Trim() -ne 'ccf3f833e32f48e583a6c6fac4796fa30756e1a4') { throw 'approved spec blob changed' }
if ($planCommit -notmatch '^[0-9a-f]{40}$') { throw 'plan is not committed' }
$planBlobRaw = & $gitExecutable -C $repositoryRoot rev-parse "$planCommit`:$planPath"
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $planBlobRaw.Trim() -cne $approvedPlanBlob) { throw 'approved plan blob crossing' }
$workingPlanBlobRaw = & $gitExecutable -C $repositoryRoot hash-object --no-filters -- $planPath
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0 -or $workingPlanBlobRaw.Trim() -cne $approvedPlanBlob) { throw 'working plan bytes differ from approved blob' }
$workingPlanSha256 = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath (Join-Path $repositoryRoot $planPath) -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
if ($workingPlanSha256 -cne $approvedPlanSha256) { throw 'approved plan SHA-256 crossing' }
& $gitExecutable -C $repositoryRoot status --short --branch
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'cannot inspect planning worktree status' }
```

Expected: branch is based on the approved baseline, the plan has a real containing commit, and only the explicitly active worktree exists in addition to root.

function deepFreeze(value) {
  if (value && typeof value === 'object' && !Object.isFrozen(value)) {
    for (const child of Object.values(value)) deepFreeze(child)
    Object.freeze(value)
  }
  return value
}

`dynamicEvidencePolicy`のproduct/UAT/final-attestation schemaVersion、index kind、directoryは`FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` sliceまでopaqueなforward declarationに限る。Wave 0Aはそのcontent schema、producer、parser、campaign publication/recovery、CLI、process authority、fixtureを実装しない。これらはWave 0A runtimeの`KnownAttachmentSchema`、`AttachmentPayload`、event payload、transaction role、campaign-index unionへ入らず、現在のCLIへ渡された場合はunknown schema/operationとして拒否する。`FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` detailed planは`PROCESSING-INTEGRITY`の`VERIFIED` exact mainを再監査し、同じopaque identifiersを変更せずにcontent schemas、producer/parser/validator、external publication/recovery、fixtures、Program-index/status linkageを通常のplan-authoring／implementation／campaign approvalで実装する。そのsliceが`VERIFIED`になるまでproduct mainをfreezeせず、4つのrepository-non-mutating phasesを開始しない。

Validate the exact top-level and nested keys recursively; `classification` is `mandatory` for all eight current boundaries. Every conditional deferred capability has exactly `sequenceAfter:['FINAL-VALIDATION']` and `requiresSeparateCampaignApproval:true`; eligibility additionally requires an indexed terminal `VERIFIED` result for every mandatory boundary through `FINAL-VALIDATION`, its hard dependencies, and a distinct later approval for the new campaign. Wave 0A deliberately exports no deferred-capability selector and accepts no satisfied-capability or deferred-approval CLI input. In particular, `feature-integration-approval/v1`, gate/capability runtime subjects, `feature-integration-disposition/v1`, and `NOT_APPLICABLE` event/terminal forms are unknown to every Wave 0A parser, producer, CLI, event path, manifest, and campaign-index validator. A later separately approved post-`FINAL-VALIDATION` plan must first define a purpose-discriminated GO/NOGO approval schema that binds exact Program-index and selection-ledger identities, authority main, predecessor terminal heads, decision, subject, activation evidence, ordered request/approval messages, `CanonicalUtc` freshness/expiry, nonce, `maxUses:1`, and the consuming campaign/attempt; it must then define the evidence-bearing selector and stale/cross-authority/replay rejection before adding eligibility or `NOT_APPLICABLE`. Until that schema and validator exist, every conditional or `rejected_current_snapshot` capability is mechanically ineligible; scalar ID arrays are never authority. The tracked projection path is authorization for a later evidence-publication boundary and is not created in Wave 0A. `create-feature-integration-program-index.mjs` must read committed bytes with `git cat-file blob $blobOid`, compute SHA-256 over those exact bytes, reject a dirty authority document, and use `open(path, 'wx')` for first creation. `--verify-existing` must recompute identities and compare canonical bytes without writing.

Implement the declared functions in the same Task 1 commit, not in a later task:

```js
function compareCodePoints(left, right) {
  const a = Array.from(left, character => character.codePointAt(0))
  const b = Array.from(right, character => character.codePointAt(0))
  for (let index = 0; index < Math.min(a.length, b.length); index += 1) {
    if (a[index] !== b[index]) return a[index] - b[index]
  }
  return a.length - b.length
}

function canonicalJson(value) {
  const ancestors = new Set()
  function render(current) {
    if (current === null) return 'null'
    if (typeof current === 'boolean') return current ? 'true' : 'false'
    if (typeof current === 'string') return JSON.stringify(current.normalize('NFC'))
    if (typeof current === 'number') {
      if (!Number.isSafeInteger(current)) throw new TypeError('noncanonical number')
      return Object.is(current, -0) ? '0' : String(current)
    }
    if (typeof current !== 'object') throw new TypeError('unsupported JSON value')
    if (ancestors.has(current)) throw new TypeError('cyclic JSON value')
    if (Reflect.ownKeys(current).some(key => typeof key === 'symbol')) throw new TypeError('symbol key')
    ancestors.add(current)
    try {
      if (Array.isArray(current)) {
        const ownKeys = Reflect.ownKeys(current)
        const expectedKeys = Array.from({ length: current.length }, (_, index) => String(index)).concat('length')
        if (ownKeys.length !== expectedKeys.length || expectedKeys.some(key => !ownKeys.includes(key))) {
          throw new TypeError('sparse or extended array')
        }
        const items = expectedKeys.slice(0, -1).map(key => {
          const descriptor = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(current, key)
          if (!descriptor?.enumerable || !Object.hasOwn(descriptor, 'value')) throw new TypeError('accessor or hidden array item')
          return render(descriptor.value)
        })
        return `[${items.join(',')}]`
      }
      const prototype = Object.getPrototypeOf(current)
      if (prototype !== null && prototype !== Object.prototype) throw new TypeError('non-plain object')
      const descriptors = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptors(current)
      const entries = Object.entries(descriptors).map(([key, descriptor]) => {
        if (!descriptor.enumerable || !Object.hasOwn(descriptor, 'value')) throw new TypeError('accessor or hidden property')
        return [key.normalize('NFC'), descriptor]
      })
      const normalizedKeys = entries.map(([key]) => key)
      if (new Set(normalizedKeys).size !== normalizedKeys.length) throw new TypeError('duplicate normalized key')
      entries.sort(([left], [right]) => compareCodePoints(left, right))
      return `{${entries.map(([key, descriptor]) => `${JSON.stringify(key)}:${render(descriptor.value)}`).join(',')}}`
    } finally {
      ancestors.delete(current)
    }
  }
  return Buffer.from(`${render(value)}\n`, 'utf8')
}

function assertExactBaselinePrerequisites(actual, expected) {
  const actualBytes = canonicalJson(actual)
  const expectedBytes = canonicalJson(expected)
  if (!actualBytes.equals(expectedBytes)) throw new TypeError('baseline prerequisite oracle mismatch')
}

function assertCanonicalOracle(actual, expected, label) {
  if (!canonicalJson(actual).equals(canonicalJson(expected))) throw new TypeError(`${label} oracle mismatch`)
}

function assertExactProgramAtomicSlices(actual, expected) {
  assertCanonicalOracle(actual, expected, 'program atomic slices')
}

function assertExactDownstreamProtocolPolicy(actual, expected) {
  assertCanonicalOracle(actual, expected, 'downstream protocol policy')
}

function assertExactDeferredCapabilities(actual, expected) {
  assertCanonicalOracle(actual, expected, 'deferred capabilities')
}

function validateProgramIndex(index) {
  assertExactKeys(index, PROGRAM_INDEX_KEYS)
  assertExactAuthorityDocuments(index.authorityDocuments)
  assertExactBaselinePrerequisites(index.baselinePrerequisites, BASELINE_PREREQUISITES)
  assertExactBoundaryArray(index.planBoundaries, PROGRAM_BOUNDARIES)
  assertExactProgramAtomicSlices(index.programAtomicSlices, PROGRAM_ATOMIC_SLICES)
  assertExactDownstreamProtocolPolicy(index.downstreamProtocolPolicy, DOWNSTREAM_PROTOCOL_POLICY)
  assertExactDeferredCapabilities(index.deferredCapabilities, DEFERRED_CAPABILITIES)
  assertAcyclicDependencies(index.baselinePrerequisites, index.planBoundaries, index.deferredCapabilities)
  assertExactArchiveAndTrustIdentities(index)
  assertExactStaticAndDynamicEvidencePolicy(index)
  rejectForbiddenDynamicKeysRecursively(index)
  return structuredClone(index)
}

```

const EXPECTED_SHA_EXPRESSION = '${{ inputs.expectedHeadSha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}'

	  '        description: Exact 40-character commit SHA to check out and verify',

	  '        type: string'
].join('\n')

	  '      campaignNonce:',
	  '        description: Exact Wave 0A dispatch correlation nonce',
	  '        required: true',
	  '        type: string'
].join('\n')

const CHECKOUT_WITH_REF_BLOCK = [
  '      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5',

].join('\n')
const VERIFY_BLOCK = [

  '        shell: bash',
  '        env:',
  `          EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA: ${EXPECTED_SHA_EXPRESSION}`,
  '        run: |',
  '          set -euo pipefail',
  '          [[ "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]',
  '          actual_head="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"',
  '          test "$actual_head" = "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA"'
].join('\n')
const REPOSITORY_STEP = [
  '      - name: Run repository check',
  '        run: node scripts/check.js'
].join('\n')
const VALID_WORKFLOW = [
	  'name: Fixture',
	  DISPATCH_RUN_NAME,
	  'on:',
  '  pull_request:',
  '  push:',
  DISPATCH_INPUT_BLOCK,
  'jobs:',
  '  check:',
  '    name: Check',
  '    runs-on: ubuntu-latest',
  '    steps:',
  CHECKOUT_WITH_REF_BLOCK,
  VERIFY_BLOCK,
  REPOSITORY_STEP,
  ''
].join('\n')
const VALID_NORMALIZED_WORKFLOW_CONTRACT = {
  id: 'fixture',
  path: 'fixture.yml',
  allowedEvents: ['pull_request', 'push', 'workflow_dispatch'],
	  dispatchInputs: [
	    { name: 'expectedHeadSha', required: true, type: 'string' },

	  ],
	  dispatchRunName: 'wave0a-${{ inputs.expectedHeadSha }}-${{ inputs.campaignNonce }}',
  expectedShaExpression: EXPECTED_SHA_EXPRESSION,
  verificationStepName: 'Verify exact checked-out commit',
  jobs: [{ jobId: 'check', runsOn: 'ubuntu-latest', displayNames: ['Check'], verificationShell: 'bash' }]
}

function replaceOnce(text, before, after) {
  assert.equal(text.split(before).length, 2, `mutation source must occur once: ${before}`)
  return text.replace(before, after)
}

for (const [name, mutate, expectedCode] of [
	  ['missing dispatch input', (text) => replaceOnce(text, DISPATCH_INPUT_BLOCK, '  workflow_dispatch:'), 'MISSING_DISPATCH_INPUT'],
	  ['optional dispatch input', (text) => replaceOnce(text, EXPECTED_HEAD_INPUT_BLOCK, EXPECTED_HEAD_INPUT_BLOCK.replace('        required: true', '        required: false')), 'INVALID_DISPATCH_INPUT'],
	  ['missing campaign nonce', (text) => replaceOnce(text, '\n      campaignNonce:\n        description: Exact Wave 0A dispatch correlation nonce\n        required: true\n        type: string', ''), 'MISSING_DISPATCH_NONCE'],
	  ['wrong dispatch run name', (text) => replaceOnce(text, DISPATCH_RUN_NAME, 'run-name: Fixture'), 'INVALID_DISPATCH_RUN_NAME'],
  ['implicit checkout', (text) => replaceOnce(text, CHECKOUT_WITH_REF_BLOCK, '      - uses: actions/checkout@34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5'), 'IMPLICIT_CHECKOUT'],
  ['merge ref checkout', (text) => replaceOnce(text, `          ref: ${EXPECTED_SHA_EXPRESSION}`, '          ref: ${{ github.ref }}'), 'INVALID_CHECKOUT_REF'],
  ['verification after repository code', (text) => replaceOnce(text, `${VERIFY_BLOCK}\n${REPOSITORY_STEP}`, `${REPOSITORY_STEP}\n${VERIFY_BLOCK}`), 'VERIFY_ORDER'],
  ['missing lowercase sha validation', (text) => replaceOnce(text, '          [[ "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]\n', ''), 'MISSING_SHA_FORMAT_CHECK'],
  ['ignored comparison', (text) => replaceOnce(text, '          test "$actual_head" = "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA"', '          test "$actual_head" = "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" || true'), 'NON_FAIL_CLOSED_VERIFY'],

  })
}

- [ ] **Step 5: Add immediate fail-closed verification to Linux jobs**

Immediately after each checkout, before setup-node or repository code:

```yaml
- name: Verify exact checked-out commit
  shell: bash
  env:
    EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
    EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.expectedHeadSha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    [[ "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]
    if [[ "$EVENT_NAME" == "workflow_dispatch" ]]; then
      test "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA" = "$GITHUB_SHA"
    fi
    actual_head="$(git rev-parse HEAD)"
    test "$actual_head" = "$EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA"
    printf 'CI_VERIFIED_HEAD_SHA=%s\n' "$actual_head" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
```

- [ ] **Step 6: Add immediate fail-closed verification to Windows jobs**

```yaml
- name: Verify exact checked-out commit
  shell: pwsh
  env:
    EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
    EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA: ${{ inputs.expectedHeadSha || github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
  run: |
    if ($env:EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA -cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{40}$') { throw 'invalid expected head SHA' }
    if ($env:EVENT_NAME -eq 'workflow_dispatch' -and $env:EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA -cne $env:GITHUB_SHA) {
      throw 'dispatch ref head does not match expected head SHA'
    }
    $actualHeadRaw = git rev-parse HEAD
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'cannot resolve checked-out commit' }
    $actualHead = $actualHeadRaw.Trim()
    if ($actualHead -cne $env:EXPECTED_HEAD_SHA) { throw 'checked-out commit mismatch' }
    "CI_VERIFIED_HEAD_SHA=$actualHead" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Encoding utf8 -Append
```

```js
const SHA = /^[0-9a-f]{40}$/u

function resolveCheckedOutCommit(env) {
  if (env.CI_VERIFIED_HEAD_SHA === undefined) {
    if (env.GITHUB_ACTIONS === 'true' || env.CI_BASELINE_MODE !== 'explicit_local') {
      throw new Error('missing verified checkout SHA')
    }
    return normalizeEvidenceValue(env.GITHUB_SHA)
  }
  if (!SHA.test(env.CI_VERIFIED_HEAD_SHA)) throw new Error('invalid verified checkout SHA')
  return env.CI_VERIFIED_HEAD_SHA
}

function collectBaseline(env = process.env, nodeVersion = process.version) {
  return {
    commit: resolveCheckedOutCommit(env),
    eventCommit: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.GITHUB_SHA),
    runId: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.GITHUB_RUN_ID),
    runAttempt: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT),
    runnerOs: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.RUNNER_OS),
    runnerArch: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.RUNNER_ARCH),
    imageOs: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.ImageOS),
    imageVersion: normalizeEvidenceValue(env.ImageVersion),
    nodeVersion: normalizeEvidenceValue(nodeVersion)
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 1: Write pure discovery and adapter RED tests**

The request is closed. `triggerBoundarySha256` binds a closed `bob-builtin-analyze/exact-head-trigger-boundary/v1` record. That record contains event/head/ref plus exactly one authenticated `create-pull-request` intent for `pull_request`, or the four ordered authenticated dispatch intents for `workflow_dispatch`. It derives an aggregate `triggerNotBefore` as the earliest `intent.createdAt` and a closed `triggerNotBeforeByWorkflow` map: PR uses the one key `pull-request`, while dispatch uses exactly the four workflow IDs and each value comes from that workflow's own authenticated intent. The dispatch variant also derives `dispatchNonceByWorkflow` from those four requests/intents and requires four distinct `SafeDispatchNonce` values; callers cannot supply the map. Every time is normalized down to a whole UTC second because GitHub REST `created_at` has second resolution:

```js
const runDiscoveryRequest = {
  schemaVersion: 'bob-builtin-analyze/exact-head-run-discovery-request/v1',
  repository: 'katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze',
  event: 'pull_request',
  expectedHeadSha: 'a'.repeat(40),
  expectedRef: 'codex/feature-integration-selection-design',

Include a third-party same-SHA dispatch before the authenticated intent, one in the same UTC second, one that becomes visible only after the intended run, and one with a wrong title; none may qualify. Exact grammar:

```text
discover-exact-head-ci-runs capture-before --repository katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze --event pull_request|workflow_dispatch --head SHA --ref REF --external-tool-authority ABSOLUTE_PATH --git-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --gh-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --output ABSOLUTE_PATH

discover-exact-head-ci-runs select-after --repository katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze --event workflow_dispatch --head SHA --ref REF --trigger-boundary ABSOLUTE_PATH --before ABSOLUTE_PATH --external-tool-authority ABSOLUTE_PATH --git-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --gh-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --output ABSOLUTE_PATH --failure-output ABSOLUTE_PATH
discover-exact-head-ci-runs verify-existing --input ABSOLUTE_PATH

`capture-before` records a closed `exact-head-run-set-snapshot/v1` with repository/event/head/ref, the complete sorted unique positive run IDs for each of the four contract workflows, observation time, and diagnostics. `select-after` verifies that exact schema and identity before use. The before-snapshot is eligible for an operation precondition and therefore can be copied durably into a create-PR or dispatch intent before the trigger. It verifies the boundary record's closed keys, mutation-intent paths/hashes, event-specific operation set/order, head/ref, and dispatch nonce/request/run-name bindings before deriving timestamps or titles; a caller-supplied clock, nonce, or title is impossible. It repeatedly fetches complete pages for at most `DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT_MS=600_000` with `POLL_INTERVAL_MS=15_000`, subtracts the authenticated before-set, and succeeds only when each workflow has exactly one new matching `run_attempt===1` candidate whose `created_at` is at or after its own boundary (`pull-request` for PR, same workflow ID for dispatch). For both event variants, zero/multiple/identity-crossed candidate closure exits `20` and creates only the event-matching closed failure output; success exits `0` and creates only discovery; producer/I/O/validation failure exits `1` with both absent. Both outputs are mandatory flags, must be absent at entry, and are mutually exclusive no-replace publications. The failure request/event and candidate arrays are bounded, run-ID sorted/unique, and preserve event/head/ref/title/time plus dispatch nonce only for dispatch, so the checkpoint is diagnostic without authorizing a retry. For dispatch, the REST object's `display_title` must be exactly `wave0a-HEAD-NONCE` using that workflow's authenticated head and nonce, and the emitted `RunSelection.dispatchNonce`/`displayTitle` must equal them. For PR, `RunSelection` forbids `dispatchNonce` and selection continues to require the separately authenticated named PR identity; its bounded `display_title` is retained only as observation. Parse and reserialize every derived time as exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ssZ`; accept `created_at === ownBoundary`, reject an earlier second, and test a valid run created later within the same source-clock second. A third-party dispatch after the earliest prior intent but before the candidate workflow's own intent must never qualify for that workflow, including same-second or delayed API visibility. Require `run.head_branch === expectedRef`. Limits are `MAX_GH_JSON_BYTES=16_777_216`, `MAX_STDERR_BYTES=1_048_576`, `MAX_DIAGNOSTICS=50`, and `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_UTF8_BYTES=512`. Tests cross both events with exits `0/20/1`, discovery/failure output presence, candidate schemas, and collision/crash prefixes. Do not wait for job success here; Task 4B verifies the selected IDs.

Every REST call uses `spawnSync(authenticatedGhAbsolutePath, ['api', '--method', 'GET', endpoint, ...])` with an empty-then-closed environment, `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, `encoding:null`, `killSignal:'SIGKILL'`, `maxBuffer:MAX_GH_JSON_BYTES + 1`, and `timeout:Math.max(1, Math.min(30_000, remainingMonotonicDeadlineMs))`. Reopen/recheck the executable identity immediately before each call. Check `error`, `signal`, integer exit status, stdout byte length, and the narrower stderr byte length before trimming or JSON parsing. A timeout, overflow, or remaining deadline of zero is terminal; it never authorizes another request. Adapter tests cover `29_999/30_000/30_001` ms per-call boundaries as well as the total polling deadline.

The `select-after` output is event-discriminated. Both variants have closed keys `schemaVersion`, `request`, `triggerBoundary`, `triggerNotBefore`, `triggerNotBeforeByWorkflow`, `beforeSnapshotSha256`, `selectedRuns`, `observedAt`, and `diagnostics`; dispatch additionally requires `dispatchNonceByWorkflow`, while PR forbids it. The time/nonce fields must equal those embedded in the fully validated boundary record; `request.triggerBoundarySha256` authenticates its canonical bytes, so no temporary locator survives in campaign evidence. `selectedRuns` is a canonical-JSON object with exactly the four contract workflow IDs as an order-independent key set; canonical serialization therefore emits code-point-sorted object keys. Each PR value is `{ runId, workflowPath, event:'pull_request', headSha, headBranch, runAttempt:1, createdAt, displayTitle }`; each dispatch value adds the exact `dispatchNonce` and has `event:'workflow_dispatch'`. Consumers validate the key set after ordinal sorting, then read the four named properties into the separate contract-order tuple; they never use property enumeration as workflow order. `runId` is a positive JavaScript-safe integer and must be distinct across the map. This exact shape is the only Task 8 source for the campaign-owned four-ID map consumed by success `assess`; no verifier `--run` values are constructed for that mode.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement the pure assessment**

The request shape is exact and closed:

```js
const exactHeadCiRequest = {
  schemaVersion: 'bob-builtin-analyze/exact-head-ci-request/v1',
  repository: 'katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze',
  mode: 'wave0a_pr_head',
  expectedHeadSha: 'a'.repeat(40),
  expectedRef: 'codex/feature-integration-selection-design',
  expectedBaseSha: 'd'.repeat(40),
  expectedBaseRef: 'main',
  pullRequestNumber: 172,
  runDiscoverySha256: 'e'.repeat(64),
  runs: {
    'extensions-quality': 123,
    'workflow-contracts': 124,
    'code-consistency-review-scaffold': 125,
    'three-extension-ui-contracts': 126
  }
}
```

Mode semantics are closed: `wave0a_pr_head` accepts `pull_request` only; future-slice `slice_pr_head` accepts the event fixed by its verified discovery record; `post_merge_main` accepts `workflow_dispatch` only. A push run may be retained as supplementary evidence but cannot satisfy a required mode. Any PR variant requires `expectedRef`, `expectedBaseSha`, `expectedBaseRef=main`, and `pullRequestNumber`, emits `event:'pull_request'`, requires 12 jobs, and forbids skipped metrics. Any dispatch variant forbids base/PR fields, emits `event:'workflow_dispatch'`, requires 11 jobs plus the exact skipped-metrics tuple; post-main additionally requires `expectedRef=main`. The adapter reopens `--run-discovery`, verifies its canonical SHA and producer schema, and derives `request.runDiscoverySha256` plus the four-ID map; callers cannot provide or reorder IDs in `assess`. A run must be completed/success, `run_attempt === 1`, match the corresponding `RunSelection` and repository/workflow/event/head/ref/title, and contain the contract-defined exact job set. Dispatch additionally requires API `display_title === wave0a-HEAD-NONCE` and exact equality with discovery's per-workflow nonce/title; PR forbids a nonce. For every job, derive the exact API label array from its static `runsOn` (`['ubuntu-latest']` or `['windows-latest']`), require canonical equality with the Jobs API `labels`, and include that array in evidence; reject `self-hosted` and any additional or missing label. Every required successful job must contain one successful `Verify exact checked-out commit` step. Do not require every step to succeed because matrix jobs contain intentional skipped steps. For either dispatch mode, the authenticated discovery nonce/title, successful static verification step, and `run.head_sha === request.expectedHeadSha` prove the requested workflow/head/ref chain; the API adapter does not claim that the Actions run endpoint exposes dispatch input values directly.

- [ ] **Step 5: Implement the explicit-run GitHub adapter**

Exact grammar:

```text
verify-exact-head-ci assess --repository katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze --mode MODE --head SHA --ref REF [--base SHA --base-ref main --pull-request NUMBER] --run-discovery ABSOLUTE_CAMPAIGN_PATH --wait-seconds 1800 --external-tool-authority ABSOLUTE_PATH --git-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --gh-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --output ABSOLUTE_PATH --partial-output ABSOLUTE_PATH
verify-exact-head-ci observe-partial --repository katamor1/bob_builtin_analyze --mode MODE --head SHA --ref REF [--base SHA --base-ref main --pull-request NUMBER] [--run workflowId=NUMERIC_ID] [--run-discovery ABSOLUTE_CAMPAIGN_PATH] --external-tool-authority ABSOLUTE_PATH --git-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --gh-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --output ABSOLUTE_PATH
verify-exact-head-ci verify-existing --input ABSOLUTE_PATH
```

When `observe-partial --run-discovery` is present, it reopens the campaign-owned discovery and requires exact mode/event/head/ref plus supplied run-ID equality before marking a dispatch correlation verified; nonce and display title come only from that record. The flag is allowed only for a dispatch mode, occurs at most once, and cannot be paired with PR-only correlation. Tests reject duplicate discovery flags, PR/discovery crossing, wrong event/head/ref/run ID, nonce/title crossing, and a discovery not contained in the authenticated campaign.

For PR modes, require all three bracketed fields and query that PR separately; do not trust `run.pull_requests`, which can be empty for a valid PR run. For post-main, forbid them. `assess` accepts exactly one campaign-owned discovery path and no `--run` flags. It no-follow proves both output paths absent before the first poll and has closed exits: `0=success`, `20=poll_exhausted`, `21=terminal_non_success`, and `1=producer_or_identity_or_io_failure`. Exit 0 atomically creates only the success `ExactHeadCiAttachment`; exit 20 atomically creates only `PartialRunAttachment{assessment:'poll_exhausted'}`; exit 21 atomically creates only `PartialRunAttachment{assessment:'terminal_non_success'}` after at least one causally selected run or required job reaches a terminal non-success conclusion. Exit 1 leaves both initially absent paths absent. A pre-existing collision leaves that path byte-identical and returns 1; a crash prefix is not an orderly typed exit and enters authenticated recovery. No exit may create both outputs, a success-shaped attachment cannot carry a non-success, and an in-progress/missing observation cannot be classified terminal. `observe-partial` is read-only and never accepts a wait/retry flag: it records each contract workflow as missing or present and each required job as missing or present with its current/terminal status and nullable conclusion, preserving failed/cancelled/skipped/timed-out/in-progress evidence instead of fabricating the success-only `RunSelection`/`JobEvidence` types. It derives `assessment:'terminal_non_success'` iff a selected run or required job is terminal non-success; otherwise it derives `poll_exhausted`. It permits zero through four unique run flags plus an optional verified discovery path. A present PR run forbids dispatch correlation. A present dispatch run stores `{status:'verified',nonce}` only when it matches that discovery; without one it stores `{status:'unverified'}` and never a nullable/fabricated nonce. It rejects any non-contract workflow or duplicate, queries each supplied positive run ID exactly once, and writes only the failure/checkpoint shape. Use `spawnSync(authenticatedGhAbsolutePath, ['api', '--method', 'GET', endpoint, ...])` with an empty-then-closed environment, `shell:false`, `windowsHide:true`, `encoding:null`, `killSignal:'SIGKILL'`, `maxBuffer:MAX_GH_JSON_BYTES + 1`, and `timeout:Math.max(1, Math.min(30_000, remainingMonotonicDeadlineMs))`. Recheck executable identity immediately before each call. Check `error`, `signal`, integer exit status, raw stdout bytes, and the narrower raw stderr cap before any trim/JSON parsing. Poll only the four IDs derived from discovery for at most `1_800_000` ms with `15_000` ms interval, fetch jobs with `per_page=100`, require complete pagination, and reject stdout above `16_777_216` bytes, stderr above `1_048_576` bytes, more than 100 jobs per run, more than 50 diagnostics, or any NFC-normalized diagnostic above `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_UTF8_BYTES=512`. An exhausted remaining deadline produces exit 20 without one more request; process timeout, overflow, identity drift, malformed data, or other producer failure produces exit 1 without semantic output. Tests cover per-call `29_999/30_000/30_001` ms, every exit/output-presence combination, and crash/collision prefixes. Never call `gh run rerun`, `gh workflow run`, merge, or delete from this CLI.

Both Task 4 adapters use this literal boundary matrix; each row is a named table-driven test, not the phrase “test the limit”:

| Dimension | N-1 | N | N+1 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| REST pages, `N=10` | page 9 accepted | page 10 accepted and complete | request/response requiring page 11 rejected before use |
| runs or jobs per page, `N=100` | 99 accepted | 100 accepted | 101 rejected |
| discovery polls, `N=40` | poll 39 may continue | poll 40 may produce the sole success or timeout | poll 41 is never issued |
| CI polls, `N=120` | poll 119 may continue | poll 120 may produce the sole success or timeout | poll 121 is never issued |
| stdout, `N=16_777_216` bytes | 16,777,215 accepted | 16,777,216 accepted | 16,777,217 rejected and no JSON parsed |
| stderr, `N=1_048_576` bytes | 1,048,575 accepted | 1,048,576 accepted | 1,048,577 rejected |
| diagnostics, `N=50` | 49 accepted | 50 accepted | 51 rejected |
| diagnostic text, `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_UTF8_BYTES=512` after NFC/single-line validation | 511 UTF-8 bytes accepted | 512 UTF-8 bytes accepted | 513 UTF-8 bytes rejected |

The fake monotonic clock fixes discovery observations at `599_999/600_000/600_001` ms and CI observations at `1_799_999/1_800_000/1_800_001` ms. Equality is the final allowed observation, never authority for one more sleep/request. `MAX_JOB_PAGES=10` is explicit; incomplete `Link` pagination at page 10 rejects rather than truncating.

The diagnostic boundary fixture is shared by every producer and every consumer that emits or validates `Diagnostic`: after NFC and one-line validation, `'界'.repeat(170) + 'a'` is exactly 511 UTF-8 bytes and is accepted, the `+'aa'` form is exactly 512 and is accepted, and the `+'aaa'` form is exactly 513 and is rejected. ASCII and non-BMP companion rows exercise the same `N-1/N/N+1` byte counts. Source tests forbid `.length`, code-point count, or a constant named `MAX_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS` as the acceptance predicate.

It can neither run generated cleanup nor seal the attempt, and has no automatic successor: only a separately approved new baseline/attempt may supersede it. `MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED` and every later merge profile require distinct `M`, the exact preparation, parents `[B,H]`, and `tree(M)=tree(H)`. The integration post-observer's ordinary two-ref outcomes are applied exactly at `main=M/feature=absent` and not-applied exactly at `main=B/feature=H`. A third live-main OID is accepted only as `post_integration_main_drift` when the same immutable observation sequence first proves `main=M/feature=absent`, later proves `main=K/feature=absent`, and proves `K != B,M` plus `M` ancestor of `K`; every other mixed or third-OID state is contradictory. Both require the exact applied integration reconciliation and matching typed settlement. Neither can claim `MERGED`, repoll, retry the push, recreate the branch, or run automatic rollback. The ordinary checkpoint-only post-main failure entry is exactly one of `POST_MERGE_CI_AMBIGUOUS`, `POST_MERGE_CI_FAILED`, `POST_MERGE_DISPATCH_FAILED`, or `POST_MERGE_RUN_DISCOVERY_FAILED`; each starts from remote-main-only `M/M/B`, then converges directly on `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED -> POST_MERGE_FAILURE_ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED -> POST_MERGE_FAILURE_FEATURE_WORKTREE_REMOVED -> POST_MERGE_FAILURE_LOCAL_MAIN_ONLY`. Every stable observation serializes the closed repository settings, archive refs, normalized statuses, prune output, complete worktrees, complete OPEN PRs, and named PR. Its top claim binds approval/request hash, `maxUses:1`, candidate, procedure, bundle, seven targets, fixed ordinal layouts, and claim-directory identity. Concurrent install, replacement, or extra child rejects before spawn. For each ordinal, create the child suspended under Task 6E kill-on-close supervision, then create-new/sync/reopen the journal pre-spawn claim containing exact executable/argv/env/CWD/outputs and supervisor/child PID/creation time. Publish the durable resume-intent record as the immediately preceding action before `ResumeThread`; only then resume. Ordinal 1 invokes the reviewed external seed procedure; before creating/loading pwsh the launcher opens that exact `-File` no-follow with non-inheritable `FILE_READ_DATA|FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES|SYNCHRONIZE`, share exactly `FILE_SHARE_READ`, authenticates identity/SHA from the same handle, and holds it through child exit plus stdout/stderr settlement. Ordinal 2 invokes only installed seed-held `wave0a-stage-minus-one create-credential-authority`, which also creates the authority-owned GitHub lifecycle retirement root. No invocation imports worktree code or uses `PATH`. Nonzero/semantic failure produces that ordinal's terminal failure seal and stops before later ordinals.

Crash recovery reopens the same claim directory and two journals. If an ordinal has no durable resume intent, owner-death proof plus kill-on-close settlement and exact absence of every bound output proves it never applied; only then may the same ordinal launch once under the same claim. If resume intent exists without the exact result/output closure, it never respawns: recovery either reconciles/adopts one uniquely proved exact result or publishes that ordinal's ambiguous/noncontinuable failure seal. A result/receipt proves applied and advances only to the next ordinal. A terminal seal, gap, replacement, unknown process outcome, non-prefix, or expired identity forbids continuation. Once both ordinal results verify, publish the provisioning result binding claim-directory identity, exact ordered ordinal result identities, derived authority, bundle, and deterministic `completedAt` copied from credential authority. Collision adopts only byte-identical canonical result bytes.

The loader exclusive-creates the authority root, 15 coordination files, campaign-publisher claim root, controller-release root, `github-lifecycle-retirement-v1` root, installed loader/bootstrap/bundle/manifest, sanitized config, credential inventory/probes, credential authority JSON, and sidecar. It reopens every member and derives the exact nine-key `Wave0aBoundControlAuthority`; `githubLifecycleRetirementRootIdentity` must equal the credential-authority member and cannot be caller-selected. Tests crash before claim install, before/after each pre-spawn claim and resume intent, during result/termination/failure-seal publication, at both ordinal boundaries, and before provisioning result. They assert one claim directory, one use, exact monotone recovery, zero respawn after ambiguous resume, same seed-procedure handle from before interpreter creation through child exit, all seven target crossings, complete held final-`H` bundle identity, lifecycle retirement root identity, and either canonical result or durable noncontinuable seal.

- [ ] **Step 4: Enforce lifecycle-before-campaign ordering and hand off the bound authority**

Before creating Task 6H lifecycle request bytes, require one separately provisioned existing disposable repository and launch `eligibility-preflight` only through Task 6E `invoke-pre-campaign --entrypoint-role lifecycle`, whose supervisor holds every installed bundle member through child exit. A missing/ineligible/already-retired repository yields `BLOCKED_PENDING_DISPOSABLE_REPOSITORY`; no code creates or configures it. The request embeds the complete 9-key `controlAuthority`, exact eligibility identity, normalized repository identity, authority-derived retirement slot, and acceptance output; its CLI accepts no claim path or raw tool/loader authority. Obtain the separate lifecycle approval, atomically install its claim directory before any spawn, and either complete/reverify under the same journal or recover an owner-death-proved exact no-seal prefix. Semantic failure/ambiguity/timeout/non-success is terminally sealed and requires a different repository. Only after acceptance bytes bind claim, journal head, retirement slot, seal absence, and lifecycle expiry may Task 6F create `Wave0aCampaignExecutionApprovalRequest` v2 through a separately held proposal launch. It embeds the byte-identical authority, lifecycle approval identity, acceptance `FileIdentity`, acceptance-derived `lifecycleExpiresAt`, and `attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`. Then—and only then—obtain campaign approval. Tests reject any worktree entrypoint, partial/early code-handle release, request before eligibility, campaign request before completed acceptance, crossed journal/slot/seal/expiry/authority identities, repository reuse, or direct Task 7 admission without all gates.

Task 6I has no Git staging or commit step. Retain the request, approval, consumption claim directory and both ordinal journals/seals, seed, authority, installed bundle, provisioning result, lifecycle claim directory/journal/seal, and lifecycle evidence until the Wave 0A attempt and every required recovery/verification path are terminally sealed.
