
Operation reservation `slotOrdinal` is the contiguous array position `1..slotCount`; it is never reused as a claim, proof, cleanup, program, or worktree-progress ordinal. Each record-specific ordinal and canonical final leaf must agree independently. Slot order is claim, every still-missing progress leaf in ascending order, then result; a proof-only plan has exactly one proof slot and a no-spawn plan exactly one claim slot. Generated cleanup permits `remainingProgressRange:null` or exactly `{first,last}` within `1..98`; root fast-forward permits `null` or one exact contiguous range within `1..(2+materializationChunkCount)`, where `materializationChunkCount` is `0..16` and the total progress count is at most `18`; worktree removal permits `null` or one exact range inside `1..min(16,ceil(entryCount/1024))`. `null` means all progress is already durable and reserves `[claim,result]`, so the full-progress/result-absent crash window is representable. In that window the spawned reconciler claim carries respectively `nextChunkOrdinal:null`, `nextStepOrdinal:null`, or `nextDeleteOrdinal:null`, executes no delete/Git mutation, revalidates the complete immutable progress prefix, and publishes only the missing process result. A non-null next ordinal is mandatory whenever any progress leaf is absent; specifically, root `nextStepOrdinal` is the exact first missing `RootFastForwardProgressOrdinal` in the full legal `1..18` range, not a `1|2` command-only shortcut. Worktree path, slot, record, descriptor, and lock all rederive the same canonical four-digit chunk ordinal; generated/worktree removal records cover their immutable 1,024-entry-or-final chunk, and each root-progress record agrees with the materialization plan's CAS/chunk/final-verification table. The slots must equal the declared range exactly—no gap, duplicate, extra progress, or zero/negative range. Reservation, claim, and actual lock/descriptor tests accept root `nextStepOrdinal` at `1/2/3/17/18/null`, table-drive every intermediate ordinal, and reject `0/19` plus a value that is not the first missing progress leaf.

Operation descriptors have two aggregate cardinality classes. `reserve_intent.members` is exactly `[request, ...ordered preconditions, intent]`, where request is first, the operation/profile table fixes 1..7 numbered preconditions, and intent is the commit member staged and published last. `publish_receipt.members` is exactly `[...ordered postconditions, receipt]`, where the operation/profile table fixes 1..3 numbered postconditions and receipt is the commit member staged and published last. `descriptor.inputRecordSha256` equals the primary intent or receipt SHA respectively, `TransactionReceipt.publishedMembers` equals the entire descriptor ordinal/size/SHA tuple byte-for-byte and in order, and ordinary `commitMemberOrdinal` equals the final member ordinal. Existing-root `begin_with_handoff` is the sole separately typed exception: `ExistingRootBeginWithHandoffMemberTuple` starts with the precomputed `attempt_started` campaign-index member at ordinal `0001`, then marker, five attachments, READY event, READY handoff, and the `operator_handoff` index member; its receipt retains the final tuple member in `commitMemberOrdinal`, separately fixes `admissionCommitMemberOrdinal:'0001'`, and uses the crash-history-independent `completionMode:'admission_canonical'` in both uninterrupted and recovered suffix completion. New-campaign begin keeps `NewCampaignBeginWithHandoffMemberTuple` in the complete-root layout and forbids an admission member ordinal because the atomic root rename is its admission commit. Claim/result/proof/progress descriptors and `publish_run_discovery` are distinct exact singleton classes. Native singletons bind `inputRecordSha256 === publicationReservationSha256`, descriptor/lock/reservation transaction identity, and the one slot. Run discovery instead binds source SHA, verified-handoff SHA, current event/index, phase-discriminated head/ref/event, role `run_discovery`, ordinal/commit `0001`, and the one derived attachment leaf; it has no native reservation. For every variant, the consumer regenerates the one legal staged and final path tuple from scope, attempt/recovery/operation owner, operation discriminator, transaction ID, member ordinal, role, and static evidence contract; no serialized member or receipt may supply a path. Every descriptor variant and record byte set cross-validates its closed authority. A missing/extra/reordered member, early/wrong admission or final commit ordinal, ordinal-label-derived-path mismatch, role/schema alias, different input hash, or lock/slot/descriptor transaction crossing rejects before canonical installation and remains recoverable only from the intact exact transaction staging.

`WorktreeRegistryFence` is the only accepted live worktree-registry/HEAD fence; the legacy `LocalWorktreeSetFencePlan` name has no type or parser. Its `feature_and_root` arm binds the common-Git and `worktrees` directories, the primary-root common-Git admin directory and `HEAD`, the linked feature admin directory and `HEAD`, and two distinct files with non-interchangeable semantics: `featureWorktreeGitFile` is the linked worktree root's `.git` file, while `featureAdminGitdirBackpointer` is the admin directory's `gitdir` backpointer. Its `root_only` arm binds the common/root identities plus both a no-follow `featureWorktreeAbsenceProof` for the former worktree path and a no-follow `featureAdminDirectoryAbsenceProof` for its former registration directory; it forbids every live feature-admin/`.git`/`gitdir`/`HEAD` identity. A real Windows no-follow probe detects registration add/move/remove/prune and either HEAD retarget and retains every opened identity from final validation through durable operation receipt. The approved local scope, `RootFastForwardPlan`, fast-forward request, root-materialization plan, and every root progress record require the same reverified `feature_and_root` arm. Only after the applied worktree-removal receipt may `delete-local-branch` derive a fresh `root_only` arm, and it holds that distinct fence through its own receipt; historical topology, a single absence proof, swapped `.git`/admin-`gitdir` identities, or the removed worktree's fence cannot substitute. Fixtures assert the ten-key feature arm and nine-key root-only arm exactly and reject missing, extra, or crossed registrations.

Before Stage 0 exists, no Task 6H lifecycle or Task 6F campaign-request process may name a `CandidateBootstrapResult` or ordinary `AUTHORITY_ARGS`. The only pre-campaign equality witness is the in-memory `PreCampaignControlAuthorityWitness`, reconstructed by no-follow reopening the exact Task 6I provisioning approval, durable consumption claim, completed provisioning result, credential-authority file/sidecar, and every request-bound authority-root/credential/loader/tool/config identity. It requires the result's `provisioningApprovalIdentity`, claim identity, derived `Wave0aBoundControlAuthority`, and `InstalledPreCampaignToolBundleIdentity` to agree transitively. Its public grammar slot is exactly `PRECAMPAIGN_AUTHORITY_ARGS = --control-authority-provisioning-approval ABSOLUTE_PATH --git-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH --gh-executable ABSOLUTE_PATH`; the two executable paths are equality witnesses for the rederived `controlAuthority.externalTools`, never selectors. The witness itself is not serialized and no additional caller-authored carrier file is created. However, executable code is independently fixed: Task 6I invokes each live pre-campaign mode only as authenticated authority-bound Node plus the role-matched installed final-`H` proposal or lifecycle entrypoint, and the entrypoint rechecks its own file and complete static-import tuple against the installed manifest before parsing argv. Lifecycle eligibility/request/claim/acceptance and the later campaign request bind the exact derived `Wave0aBoundControlAuthority`, whose `provisioningApprovalIdentity` is that same held approval identity. A worktree/repository/copy entrypoint, bootstrap-result flag, raw authority object/path, alternate provisioning approval, executable crossing, PATH lookup, extra/missing/reordered tuple member, or any use before the provisioning result re-verifies rejects before process launch.

A new-campaign approval request binds only `rootInstall:'atomic_first_root'`, the absent campaign-root contract, and one final-`H` `firstRootInstallPolicyIdentity` at `tools/main-consolidation/wave0a-first-root-install-policy.json`; it never embeds a future admission template, staged root, plan, or result identity. The reopened `first-root-install-policy/v1` has exactly the closed Boolean requirements and numeric bounds in `FirstRootInstallPolicy`: `16_777_216` plan bytes, `16_384` entries, depth `256`, `67_108_864` aggregate relative-path UTF-8 bytes, `1_073_741_824` per file, `17_179_869_184` total bytes, `16` chunks, `1_024` actions per chunk, and `18` progress records. After approval, `begin` creates and reopens canonical `FirstRootAdmissionTemplateRecord` bytes, derives the non-self-referential `FirstRootAdmissionTemplateIdentity{template,record}`, reserves absent canonical external `FirstRootInstallPlanTarget` and `BeginAdmissionCommitResultTarget` paths whose `parentIdentity` and safe `leaf` reconstruct `canonicalPath`, requires both new-mode targets to share the exact no-follow-held original result-artifact parent (while existing mode has only the result target), and writes the immutable result-first `BeginResult` binding that wrapper and both targets without final hashes. Inside `admitBeginAtomically`, after sampling `recordedAt` and finalizing/reopening every dependent byte, the process-free plan builder creates `FirstRootInstallPlan` at its bound target with `createdAt === commitBinding.recordedAt`, that byte-identical policy identity, the still-absent destination, the admission-template wrapper, `FinalizedReadyStagedRootIdentity`, one same-volume atomic publish action, and only `PlannedRenamed*Identity` projections from each live staged-root source identity to its still-absent destination path. Those projections are explicitly non-authoritative and never claim a destination `FileIdentity` or `DirectoryHandleIdentity` before rename; the actual installed identities appear first in the postcommit `BeginAdmissionCommitResult`. The three staged transient-absence proofs likewise become `PlannedFirstRootTransientAbsenceProof` source-proof/destination-path projections. After rename, the result carries the time-free `InstalledFirstRootTransientAbsenceIdentity`: each leaf is the exact deterministic transform of its planned source proof into the destination canonical path and retained parent directory object identity, with `observation:'absent_no_follow_at_publish'` authorized only by the verified atomic-rename receipt. It never resamples `observedAt`, so uninterrupted completion and arbitrarily delayed recovery serialize byte-identical result content. The Stage 0 closed-binding file is not a staged-root member and is never renamed: `postPublish.initialControlBinding` is instead `PlannedUnchangedExternalClosedInitialControlBindingIdentity{disposition:'unchanged_external',sourceIdentity,contentIdentity}`, and the postcommit promotion must retain that same full external identity and content. The plan syncs, reopens, and hashes its target through the originally held `parentIdentity` before the final clock fence; result publication uses the same parent/leaf reconstruction and rejects parent replacement, a non-regular occupant, `linkCount != 1`, or any different parent handle. Exact adoption requires no-follow regular-file reopening and canonical byte equality; a byte-exact standalone copy is indistinguishable and accepted as adoption, never claimed as producer provenance. The primitive revalidates the complete plan/absence/approval/fence and syncs a `BeginWithHandoffTransactionReceipt` carrying crash-history-independent `completionMode:'admission_canonical'` and `commitDeadlineFence:'native_checked_immediately_before_publish_with_lifecycle_expiry'`; it then samples the ephemeral `commitFenceNow`, requires `recordedAt <= commitFenceNow < attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`, and calls native rename-no-replace as the immediately following statement. The second sample is never serialized. A precommit restart may remove only an exact owned plan target before resampling and rebuilding it; after canonical commit the plan target is immutable and required. Only then does the live caller or recovery deterministically create-or-exact-adopt the target `BeginAdmissionCommitResult` from the committed bytes. The begin descriptor forbids `externalResult`: its result target is already transitively bound in `beginAdmission.admissionTemplate.record`, and adding a prospective result size/hash would form a descriptor/result/receipt cycle. This placement avoids any request -> staged campaign authority -> campaign approval -> request hash cycle and prevents the atomic rename from publishing a live lock. Every existing-root template/descriptor/lock forbids `FirstRootInstallPlanTarget` and carries only `rootInstall:'existing_root_transaction'`; the two forms never coerce or recover through one another. Tests reject a fabricated destination identity, staged/destination path crossing, changed source dev/inode/content, a renamed projection outside the absent destination root, source/destination transient-proof crossing, an external binding path inside that root or any changed external identity/content, target parent/leaf/path crossing, parent replacement, non-regular or multiply-linked targets, noncanonical adoption bytes, any installed absence projection that is not the exact time-free transform of the planned proof, live-versus-delayed result byte drift, uninterrupted-versus-suffix-recovery begin-receipt byte drift, and `externalResult` on either begin descriptor arm.

Existing-root admission uses a different atomic publication point without weakening that deadline fence. Before the ephemeral sample it has staged, hashed, synced, reopened, and cross-linked all ten `ExistingRootBeginWithHandoffMemberTuple` bytes. Immediately after `approvedAt <= recordedAt <= commitFenceNow < attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`, its sole native action no-replace links/CASes the ordinal-`0001` `attempt_started` campaign-index member against the approval-bound prior head. That first canonical index entry is the admission commit and consumes the approval; the marker, five attachments, READY event, READY handoff, and final `operator_handoff` index are the descriptor-bound monotone suffix. A crash before ordinal `0001` discards the time-dependent staging and may resample; a crash after ordinal `0001` never resamples or rechecks the deadline and may only publish the exact precomputed suffix and final receipt. Until every suffix member and the receipt verify, the whole-campaign verifier exposes only the closed begin-recovery state—never a business-ready handoff, generic campaign-prefix recovery, or a second attempt. Tests crash after each canonical ordinal, require byte-exact suffix adoption, and reject changed/missing staged bytes, wrong prior head, any ordinal-`0001` replacement, deadline resampling after the first link, or use of the new-root tuple/receipt arm.

`BeginResult` is the closed seven-key canonical record `{schemaVersion,kind,mutationAuthority,campaignMode,rootInstall,admissionNonce,admissionTemplate}` under the separate 1 MiB controller-record cap. Its wrapper record transitively fixes the exact approval/request, plan/Program, candidate/local-scope/root/attempt/deadline, fixed relative-path plan, staged binding content, and create-new result target with its parent identity/safe leaf/path; only the new arm also fixes the absent destination, first-root policy, stable `stagedRoot:DirectoryHandleIdentity`, and same-parent install-plan target, while only the existing arm fixes the held campaign root, prior index head, and stable `stagedTransactionRoot:DirectoryHandleIdentity`. These two pre-admission staging identities bind the same opened directory objects only: they deliberately omit mutable mtime/ctime/entry-count/tree content that the atomic primitive has not written yet. The primitive retains and revalidates that same handle identity while it changes content; new mode records the finished content only in `FinalizedReadyStagedRootIdentity.root:DirectoryIdentity` and its tree/hash closure, while existing mode records the finished transaction only through the descriptor member tuple, reopened member identities, and receipt. A handle replacement, a pre-finalization `DirectoryIdentity` or tree hash in the template, a final snapshot of another handle, or any write outside the compound primitive rejects. The top-level mode/root-install/nonce must equal the nested record byte-for-byte. Final `attempt_started`, event/index/handoff/token/descriptor/receipt/root/installed-binding identities, `recordedAt`, `commitFenceNow`, plan/result hashes, and an optional postcommit field are unknown keys and reject. `StageHistoricalInput` names the exact begin-result schema, and `HistoricalBootstrapResult` distributes the parsed new/existing `BeginResult` across prepared, existing suffix-pending, same-mode commit-result-pending, and same-mode committed arms without widening the wrapper or result. Exact-key, nested mode/nonce/identity crossing, old/unknown schema, oversize, target collision, target-parent replacement/leaf/path crossing, same-handle/final-content crossing in both modes, and every root-status/mode/result-identity crossing test are mandatory.

`held/begin-admission-observation.json` is a distinct closed seven-key, 1 MiB Stage 0 record `{schemaVersion,mutationAuthority,beginResult,rootInstallStatus,admissionTemplateIdentity,admissionCommitIndexHead,admissionCommitResult}`. `beginResult` is the no-follow reopened `FileIdentity` of the exact original immutable `BeginResult`, not the identity of a Stage 0 copy; its parsed mode/root-install/nonce/template wrapper must equal `admissionTemplateIdentity`. Stage 0 also reopens the original `admissionTemplate.template.canonicalPath`, verifies its complete original `FileIdentity`, and requires its canonical record bytes to equal `admissionTemplate.record`. The manifest's `held/begin-admission-template.json` is only a byte-identical non-authoritative evidence copy of that record: its distinct path/inode identity can never replace or regenerate the original wrapper. The two `prepared` arms require `admissionCommitIndexHead:null`, `admissionCommitResult:null`, and one exact new- or existing-mode wrapper while canonical admission is absent. The existing-only `admission_committed_suffix_pending` arm requires the exact ordinal-`0001` `admissionCommitIndexHead`, the existing-mode wrapper, and a null result; it proves the deadline authority is consumed and permits only exact suffix recovery. After the complete new-root rename or existing-root suffix/receipt, the two `commit_result_pending` arms carry `{identity:null,result}` where `result` is the deterministically derived same-mode `BeginAdmissionCommitResult` content and the pre-bound target is still absent; only create-new/exact-adopt of those exact bytes is authorized. The two `committed` arms carry the same result with its actual target `FileIdentity`. In both latter statuses, `result.admissionCommitIndexHead` and `result.commitBinding` must equal the observation and same mode/template. `rootInstallStatus` therefore appears in both this held observation and `HistoricalBootstrapResult`, but the records are separately versioned and neither may substitute for the other. Unknown/missing keys, a changed original `BeginResult` or template identity, a held-copy identity substitution, prepared-with-head/result, pending-suffix new-mode/result, result-pending with a file identity, committed with null identity, first-head/result drift, template/nonce/mode crossing, result-target crossing, or replay from another recovery bundle rejects.

The pre-begin closed binding is likewise content-bound without a future canonical file identity. `CandidateBootstrapResult.initialControlBinding` is exactly `{relativePath:'local/Candidate/held/closed-initial-control-binding.json',contentIdentity,binding}`; `contentIdentity` exposes only schema, byte length, and SHA-256, and its bytes contain identities and policy only, never credential secret bytes. `Wave0aClosedInitialControlBinding` contains no sampled `createdAt`: every fresh launcher deterministically reconstructs the same exact closed keys from the already captured approval/acceptance/candidate identities and must reproduce byte-identical canonical content. `FirstRootAdmissionTemplateRecord` carries that same relative-path/content pair, while `FirstRootAdmissionTemplateIdentity` adds only the separately derived identity of those exact record bytes; neither record nor file hashes itself. `FinalizedReadyStagedRootIdentity` and the inside-primitive `FirstRootInstallPlan` retain that wrapper without promoting an installed binding identity. Only after the atomic-first-root install or existing-root begin transaction commits may the deterministic `BeginAdmissionCommitResult` promote the binding to `ClosedInitialControlBindingFileIdentity{fileIdentity,contentIdentity}` and be published at the pre-bound external result target. Every post-begin `OperatorHandoff`, `VerifiedHandoff`, current `BootstrapResult`, and controller-release root envelope carries that exact final pair. Historical bootstrap is a closed union: ordinary handoff/root-envelope inputs are installed-only, while a `BeginResult` is immutable authority joined to exactly one of four observations—admission absent, existing-root ordinal-`0001` committed with suffix pending, complete canonical commit with result target pending, or the same result exact-adopted at its target. It never changes its own bytes from staged to installed, never resamples after either admission-committed arm, and never exposes either pending arm as business-ready. The closed binding is a separately capped 1 MiB controller/bootstrap record, not an `AttachmentPayload` or attempt-manifest member, so the 42/42/42 registries and sixteen fixture attachments do not change.

`RootHandoffPlan` and `ControllerReleaseRequest` are closed correlated unions, not independently selectable state/profile bags. The only normal arm is exactly `MAIN_ONLY/ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED`; the only failure arm is exactly `MERGED/POST_MERGE_FAILURE_ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED`. Both require `operationReceipt` to be the owning attempt's `fast-forward-root` `recordKind:'receipt'` with schema `wave0a-mutation-receipt/v1`, and require one identical `expectedHeadSha == bootstrapRepository.expectedHeadSha == M`. The request repeats state/profile/head only inside the matching union arm and embeds the byte-identical canonical plan; validator tests reject both cartesian crossings, a generic or foreign receipt, operation/record-kind drift, head drift, a separately reconstructed plan, and every top-level/inline-plan inequality.

The static operation/profile table is also the sole canonical pre/postcondition leaf authority. Position `i` is rendered as the four-digit ordinal plus the table label, and `OperationEvidenceRef{recordKind:'precondition'|'postcondition'}` must carry that identical label, exact `SafeOperationPreconditionPath|SafeOperationPostconditionPath`, owning attempt/instance, producer schema, size, and SHA. Request, intent, claim, process-result, termination-proof, and receipt refs must use their one fixed path family and cannot alias a numbered leaf. Producer and consumer tests enumerate all 15 instances and every mode, then reject count 0/8 preconditions, count 0/4 postconditions, gaps, duplicate ordinals or labels, label/path disagreement, wrong schema, foreign attempt/instance, and a semantically valid payload installed at a noncanonical leaf.

The chain validator opens every claim/proof byte and enforces claim kind, not merely locator order. Claim 1 is exactly one of `SupervisorOperationClaim`, a spawned `ReconcilerOperationClaim` for cleanup/root-fast-forward/worktree-removal, or `NoSupervisorReconcilerClaim`; they are mutually exclusive. Claim `N>1` is only a spawned reconciler and requires claim/proof `N-1`. `no_spawn_fenced` is exactly one ordinal-1 `NoSupervisorReconcilerClaim`, no proof/result/next claim, and can never become an effective execution owner. In `proof_required`, `terminated_without_result`, and `result_durable`, `effectiveClaim` must reopen as supervisor or spawned reconciler; the no-spawn kind is forbidden. Tests cross every state with every claim kind, including an apparently well-formed link chain whose underlying claim kind is wrong.

`OperationInspectionAttachment.classification:'absent'` is legal only when request, preconditions, intent, claims/proofs/progress/result, postconditions, receipt, operation lock, every operation transaction descriptor/receipt/staged member, and every canonical aggregate prefix are all absent for that instance. Before emitting the existing three-way attachment, inspection exact-recovers a valid prepared request/precondition prefix and then emits `intent_only`, or exact-recovers a valid postcondition/receipt prefix and then emits `receipted`. A staged-only, incomplete-prepared, corrupt, or foreign state hard-stops and emits no inspection attachment; it never becomes `absent`. Tests cover both valid recoveries, every corrupt/staged-only case, and prove no such state can authorize an exit-74 pre-intent retry.

`mutation_reconciliation_required` never uses the generic normal checkpoint shape. Its serialized `reconciliationOrigin` determines the only legal fresh-session action: controller pre-claim spawn failure or historical unclaimed/terminated ordinary operation -> ordinal-1 no-spawn fence; historical unclaimed/terminated cleanup, root fast forward, or worktree removal -> deterministic same-intent suffix; any historical durable result -> read-only receipt reconciliation. `HistoricalPrecheckpointSubject` and `HistoricalOperationPrecheckpointWindow` spell these mappings as closed unions: every ordinary operation maps only to `observe_only_no_spawn`, each of the three resumable operation IDs maps only to its own named journal program, `proof_required` maps only to same-ordinal termination proof then revalidation, and owner state maps to exactly one action. The checkpoint transaction copies the exact `wave0a-supervised-operation-result/v1` preclaim failure payload or `wave0a-historical-precheckpoint-validation/v1` validation payload into an attempt-owned immutable attachment, replaces the proposal's `EvidenceSlot` with its typed campaign locator, and only then publishes the checkpoint. The checkpoint, `RecoveryAdoption`, recovered handoff, and Task 6G request must carry the byte-identical origin object and re-open that locator after every prior staging root is deleted. Any scalar-hash-only, missing, caller-selected, downgraded, operation/program/action crossing, proof/action crossing, or crossed origin rejects before proof, claim, or spawn. Producer/consumer tests enumerate every legal operation/program/owner/action row, reject the cartesian complement, delete the native/historical staging directory, rehydrate in a fresh process, and require the campaign-owned locator to remain sufficient.

Every `RecoveryCheckpoint` and `RecoveryCheckpointProposal` carries diagnostics through `RecoveryCheckpointAttachmentSetForFailure<F>` and `CheckpointDiagnosticLabelsByFailureContext[F]`; there is no generic zero/one/two tuple escape hatch. `RecoveryCheckpointProfileForContext<S,P>` distributes the state/profile before selecting the failure arm: `READY/LOCAL_GATE_FAILED_CLEANUP` is only `local_gate_failed`; the two settlement stops are only `pr_settlement_failed`; both main-drift stops are only `topology_drift`; and each of the four post-main failure-entry profiles selects its one matching failure code. Pre-merge `PR_ACTIVE/PR_ACTIVE` CI uses exactly `['partial-run']`, whereas the two post-main CI profiles use exactly `['run-discovery','partial-run']`. The discriminated checkpoint profile therefore fixes `failureCode`, exact ordered diagnostic label tuple, cleanup/reconciliation fields, and the enclosing `expectedState/resumeProfile` context together. `ReplaceEvidenceRefsWithSlots` preserves each literal diagnostic label in `attachmentLabel`, so proposal slot replacement retains that same distributed union and publication substitutes verified locators without widening it. Tests enumerate every failure/context row, both legal CI diagnostic tuples, each exact post-main dispatch prefix/locator, partial-cleanup and mutation-reconciliation arms, and reject a correct-schema diagnostic under the wrong failure code, state/profile, order, arity, label, or proposal/checkpoint phase.

`HandoffRehydration.attachments` is not an event-history bag. It is the exact unique-label carry-forward projection required for restart, and every profile carries the one immutable READY-owned `github-pr-lifecycle-acceptance`. Profile `READY` has exactly `['generated-before','github-pr-lifecycle-acceptance']`; normal profiles `LOCAL_GATE_FAILED_CLEANUP`, `LOCAL_PRE_PUBLISH`, `LOCAL_PUBLISHED`, `PR_ACTIVE`, `PREMERGE_PR_CLOSED`, `PREMERGE_READY_RESTORED`, `PREMERGE_BRANCH_DELETED_MAIN_DRIFT`, `MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED`, `MAIN_INTEGRATED_PR_PENDING`, `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED`, `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_TIMEOUT`, `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT`, `MERGED_PRE_FETCH`, `MERGED`, `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED`, and `MAIN_ONLY`, plus failure profiles `POST_MERGE_CI_AMBIGUOUS`, `POST_MERGE_CI_FAILED`, `POST_MERGE_DISPATCH_FAILED`, and `POST_MERGE_RUN_DISCOVERY_FAILED`, have exactly `['generated-after','generated-before','github-pr-lifecycle-acceptance']`; `PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED`, `GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED`, and `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` have exactly `['generated-after','generated-before','generated-cleanup','github-pr-lifecycle-acceptance']`; normal `ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED`, `FEATURE_WORKTREE_REMOVED`, and `VERIFIED`, plus failure `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED`, `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_FEATURE_WORKTREE_REMOVED`, and `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_LOCAL_MAIN_ONLY`, have exactly `['archive-preflight-final','generated-after','generated-before','generated-cleanup','github-pr-lifecycle-acceptance']`. Arrays are ordinal by label, labels are unique, and each entry reopens the one event/receipt-owned locator prescribed by the profile. Current topology exists only in `latestTopology`; the settlement and drift handoff arms additionally carry their explicitly typed reconciliation/settlement locators, while PR/main run evidence remains in its owning event/operation and is never duplicated into the generic attachment map. `Get-UniqueCampaignAttachment` is restricted to `HandoffCarryForwardLabel` and resolves only this projection, so repeated event-local slot names cannot make a handoff lookup ambiguous. Tests enumerate every profile's exact set and explicit stop-only fields and reject missing, extra, duplicate, stale, or wrong-owner entries. The acceptance locator is byte-identical across every successor and is never republished or replaced after `begin_with_handoff`.

`PreMergeFailedPayload|CompletedPostMergeFailedPayload` is the sole terminal diagnostic and outcome authority; there is no cartesian intersection among unrelated evidence, state, rollback, or main-disposition shapes. Pre-merge PR `ci_failed|ci_ambiguous` and post-main `ci_failed|ci_ambiguous` each require exactly one `partialRunEvidence` locator whose reopened payload is the checkpoint's mode-matching `PartialRunAttachment`; the surrounding last-state/DAG/profile arm distinguishes the two and forbids crossing their bytes. Post-main CI and run-discovery failure require `through_dispatch_4/receipted_applied`; each `main_dispatch_failed` arm instead couples the exact current dispatch's `not_observed|ambiguous` operation postcondition to its matching cumulative prefix and records the final entry as `receipted_not_applied|receipted_ambiguous`. Thus the elements before that last dispatch are the applied prefix (zero through three dispatches), while the failed dispatch itself is never represented as applied. Pre-merge `pr_run_discovery_failed` and post-main `main_run_discovery_failed` require the exact event-matching `RunDiscoveryFailureAttachment`. `pr_settlement_failed` belongs only to the nonterminal post-integration controlled stop and is not a `FailedPayload` failure code. Every other terminal failure code forbids all three diagnostic keys rather than accepting `null` or `undefined`. A pre-merge arm carries exactly one `LocalAbortIdentity|BranchActiveAbortIdentity|PrActiveAbortIdentity`, one legal DAG v2 entry, and only the rollback/mutation tuple fixed for that identity; the rehydration union reuses those same three identities and correlates local-only, branch-only, and PR history with their legal state, PR-number, merge-SHA, and drift profiles instead of recombining their fields. A completed post-main arm requires exact integrated `M`, integration settlement/reconciliation identities, one legal post-main entry (`through_dispatch_4/receipted_applied` for CI/discovery, or the correlated failed-dispatch entry), and the four cleanup receipts, while forbidding every abort identity/key. `FailureAttachment.failureCode`, `RecoveryCheckpoint.failureCode`, and `FailedPayload.failureCode` must be identical. Cross-product tests require exactly the mode-matching diagnostic and state/identity/entry/outcome tuple, enumerate both failed dispositions at dispatch positions one through four, reject an applied failed dispatch and a failed earlier prefix member, reject a same-schema locator outside the checkpoint, and reject every impossible event/failure crossing, `null`, extra key, or noncanonical serialized key set.

`HandoffToken` is deliberately fixed-size and has exactly the four top-level keys shown in the schema, in canonical JSON key order. It contains no path, worktree, bootstrap repository, external-tool identity, or `ToolBundleManifest`; the separately supplied/result-derived campaign root and handoff path remain nonauthority locators until token hash verification authenticates the full `OperatorHandoff`. Bootstrap bounds the Base64URL text at `595` characters, decodes at most `446` bytes, canonical-parses and re-encodes byte-identically, reopens the handoff no-follow, and verifies campaign root, derived location, candidate triple, index head, bootstrap selection, and full manifest before any blob load. The earliest legal handoff head is sequence `2`; the maximum is `5759`. Sixty-three completed attempts consume `63*(1 attempt_started + 56 operator_handoff + 32 recovery_checkpoint + 1 terminal)=5670` entries; the 64th may consume its start, 56 handoffs, and 32 checkpoints through handoff `5759`, reserving terminal `5760`. A recovery checkpoint is therefore capped at `5758` so its successor handoff and terminal still fit. `MAX_CAMPAIGN_INDEX_ENTRIES=8192` is the loose `64*128` parser/storage bound and does not make any sequence above `5760` legal. Producer, seed loader, bootstrap, recovery, and verified-output tests cover byte/token `N-1/N/N+1`, sequence `2/5759`, rejection of `1/5760/8192`, checkpoint `5758` plus successor, checkpoint `5759` rejection, and exact remaining-slot calculation before checkpoint/handoff/terminal publication. Deferred final-attestation does not reserve or publish a Wave 0A index entry.

`Get-Wave0aCheckpointCapacity -VerifiedHandoff H -ReservePostMergeClosure` is the mandatory pre-main admission oracle and is legal only at `PR_ACTIVE/MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED` before `integrate_main_exact_lease`. Its result contains the sole Boolean `canIntegrateWhilePreservingPostMergeClosure` plus one create-new `wave0a-capacity-observation/v1` path. The projection includes the two-ref integration receipt/successor, settlement/fetch and the `MERGED` event/handoff, all four dispatch operations and successors, the receipt-backed `publish-run-discovery/main` singleton, the successful exact-main-CI attachment, `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED` event/handoff, direct non-mutation `MAIN_ONLY` event/handoff, all four local cleanup successors, and the terminal entry. It separately includes the larger of one settlement-stop checkpoint/companion and one no-receipt `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT` checkpoint/companion, one dispatch- or discovery-failure checkpoint/companion, one final CI-failure checkpoint/companion, every transaction/charge peak, and one optional `mutation_reconciliation_required` checkpoint/companion for **each remaining mutation instance**: integration, fetch-after-integration, four dispatches, and four local cleanup operations. Admission uses the maximum of the complete success closure and each typed failure or controlled-stop closure; mutually exclusive branches are measured separately and the largest wins. Every projected handoff includes the already-published lifecycle-acceptance locator and its measured byte growth, but no extra operation/index entry. Attempt-start admission separately reserves the largest pre-main rejection closure for every later typed stop, including `lifecycle_acceptance_invalid` and a false capacity result: first-use preservation plus diagnostic/failure/checkpoint/companion, `close-pull-request-abort -> delete-remote-branch-abort -> cleanup-generated-paths` with all three applied successors, one optional `mutation_reconciliation_required` checkpoint/companion for each of those three abort operations, and the terminal entry. That rejection reserve is never consumed by the post-main projection. Therefore false can safely publish `capacity_insufficient` with exactly `capacity-observation` while main is still `B` and enter the existing abort suffix; it never uses `publication_failed` without a publication diagnostic and never executes integration. Pure capacity fixtures derive this branch from the semantic member generator and test its limiting counter at `N-1/N/N+1`, including the first preservation delta and five-attachment READY/handoff sizes. Every later integration, dispatch, discovery-publication, and checkpoint publisher recomputes that the unconsumed suffix—including the optional reconciliation pair for every still-unconsumed mutation—fits and may not borrow from it.

`Get-Wave0aCheckpointCapacity -VerifiedHandoff H -ReservePostMergeFailureEntry -EntryKind dispatch|run_discovery` is the mandatory post-integration entry oracle. Before each of dispatches 1..4, `dispatch` projects the currently applied prefix and takes the maximum of (a) a possible typed dispatch-failure checkpoint/companion plus the complete four-operation local-cleanup/terminal suffix and (b) all later dispatch successors, the receipt-backed discovery singleton, successful exact-main-CI attachment, `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED` event/handoff, direct `MAIN_ONLY` event/handoff, four cleanup successors, and terminal. It includes optional reconciliation checkpoint/companion pairs for the current dispatch and every mutation that remains on the measured branch. Immediately before `select-after` and `publish-run-discovery`, `run_discovery` analogously takes the maximum of its failure attachment/checkpoint/companion closure and the successful singleton/CI/events/cleanup closure, with optional reconciliation pairs for all four remaining local mutations. A false result is an integrity contradiction and performs zero writes; it never permits a dispatch or discovery that could strand `M`. Fixtures cover failure at dispatch prefix lengths 1/2/3/4, discovery failure only after exactly four dispatch receipts, the complete success closure, each capacity counter at `N-1/N/N+1`, and the exact mode-specific diagnostic/member delta.

`Get-Wave0aCheckpointCapacity -VerifiedHandoff H -ReservePostMergeFailureCleanup` is a read-only closed capacity oracle. The switch is legal only for a verified `MERGED/MERGED` handoff after the exact four-dispatch prefix. It recomputes the current attempt/campaign index heads, recovery-checkpoint count, operator-handoff count, attempt-member count, and whether the unique preservation set already exists. Its non-negotiable worst-case suffix reserve is exactly five recovery checkpoints (one final main-CI failure checkpoint plus at most one canonical mutation-reconciliation checkpoint for each of the four local cleanup operations), nine future operator handoffs (one companion for each of those five checkpoints plus the four adjacent applied-operation successors), and one terminal index entry. The member projection includes the exact final `run-discovery,partial-run` diagnostics, matching failure, fresh-or-campaign topology, the unique preservation delta when it does not yet exist, and each operation-reconciliation checkpoint's maximum legal topology/inspection/origin delta. An operation that does not need reconciliation leaves its reserved pair unused; no later retry may reclaim it. The result has exactly `canPublishReservedFailureCleanup` and `canAppendRetryCheckpointWhilePreservingFailureCleanup`: the first is true only when that complete worst-case suffix fits every per-attempt, per-campaign, global-sequence, handoff, checkpoint, and attempt-member cap; the second is true only when one additional retry checkpoint and its companion handoff also fit while leaving the first predicate true afterward. The operator may append another retry only on the second predicate, must consume the reserved final failure checkpoint on first-true/second-false, and performs zero writes on first-false because that contradicts campaign admission. No retry, checkpoint, or cleanup path may lower or borrow from this reserve. Pure and adapter fixtures cover each limiting counter and the combined index/member projection at `N-1/N/N+1`, including zero prior retry checkpoints, the last legal retry, the reserved `ci_ambiguous` checkpoint, all four optional reconciliation pairs, all four applied-operation successors, and the terminal entry. This later oracle refines retry admission only; it cannot weaken the earlier pre-main closure reserve.
Wave 0A is the sole runtime bootstrap in this plan: it requires `Wave0aDecisionAuthority`, `authorityCommitSha == READY.implementationHeadSha`, and the Program-index identity resolved by `authorityCommitSha:path`. The broader `DecisionAuthority` and `Subject` declarations document stable future field names only; their `wave0b_accepted_main`, `selection_ledger/post_wave0b`, gate, and capability branches have no Wave 0A parser, adapter, selector, fixture producer, or CLI and are rejected at every runtime boundary. A later separately approved plan may implement them only by requiring non-candidate object identities at one exact `authorityMainSha`, proving the immediately preceding indexed terminal main, regenerating ledger Markdown from JSON, and adding the fresh purpose-bound approval contract specified above. Merely reachable older commits or scalar subject IDs can never authorize that later work.

A `ProgramBoundaryId` must be the exact literal union above; a `ProgramGateId` must occur exactly once in the selected authority's gate catalog; a `SelectionLedgerCapabilityId` must occur exactly once as a primary ledger capability. Syntax alone never authorizes membership. `SourceOrigin.archive` must resolve its manifest, exact range, old PR, and source item in the ledger; `current_main` must resolve its evidence ID at the declared baseline; `new_design` must bind the ledger's `requiredSpecIdentity`, a committed approved spec, and the same explicit design approval used by `READY` before an attempt can begin. Evidence labels match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`, but path ownership is not interchangeable: `owner:'attempt'` paths are relative to the owning attempt root and match only `attachments/NNNN-LABEL.EXT`, while `owner:'operation'` paths are campaign-root-relative and match only one literal `operations/ATTEMPT_ID/OPERATION_INSTANCE_ID/...` leaf in `SafeOperationEvidencePath`. For operation evidence, `recordKind` maps bijectively to `request.json`, `intent.json`, `claims/NNNN.json`, `process-result.json`, `termination-proofs/NNNN.json`, the pre/postcondition subtrees, or `receipt.json`. Claim ordinals are gap-free and every termination proof has the exact same ordinal and digest-bound claim; extra tails, forks, or scalar effective-claim shortcuts are forbidden. The attempt ID, operation instance, label, producer schema, and path must all agree. Owner/path/kind/schema crossings are hard rejects. Attachment validators open content, validate the declared schema, and cross-check head/base/PR/run/merge/topology identities rather than trusting only hashes.

State payload ownership is exact. New evidence created by the `READY`, `LOCAL`, `PR_ACTIVE`, and `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED` event transactions is attempt-owned. In `MERGED`, `integrationReconciliation` and `integrationSettlement` are operation-owned while `topology` is attempt-owned. In `MAIN_ONLY`, `integrationMutation` is an operation locator, `integrationReconciliation` reopens the `integrate-main-exact-lease` postcondition that proves feature absence, and `topology` is attempt-owned; no later remote-deletion field exists. In Wave 0A `VERIFIED`, `finalTopology` is attempt-owned, whereas `generatedCleanup` and `archivePreflight` reopen operation-owned postcondition or precondition evidence. Only `completionProfile:'standard'` is legal; product/UAT/raw-artifact/final-attestation input is an unknown operation and rejects. `FAILED` recovery fields may use either owner only where the closed failure prefix names that producer; `latestTopology` may therefore be operation-owned. Every state validator enforces this exact key/owner table rather than accepting the broad `CampaignOwnedEvidenceRef` union by shape.

Approval-message normalization is exact: strict UTF-8 decode, Unicode NFC, convert CRLF and lone CR to LF, preserve every other code point, then compute `SHA-256(UTF8(normalizedText))`. Every implementation, control-authority provisioning, disposable-lifecycle, campaign, attempt-tree-quarantine, and campaign-publication-quarantine approval uses the one provider-backed closed `TrustedApprovalTranscript`: source `codex_trusted_transcript_v1`, one `CodexThreadId`, and strictly increasing `assistantAnnouncement -> assistantPrompt -> userApproval` messages whose nested source/thread/role agree with the container. The assistant announcement names the exact plan or canonical request SHA, the assistant prompt is the exact requested approval literal, and only a later distinct `role:'user_approval'` message with byte-identical normalized prompt text grants that approval; assistant self-echo, cross-thread copy, role substitution, missing prompt, same/reversed ordinal/time, prefix/suffix, digest/text crossing, or replay rejects. `ApprovalInstructionIdentity` is v4, campaign request/approval are v2, lifecycle request/approval are v2/v3, provisioning request/approval are v1, and both quarantine request/approval pairs are v2 with `maxUses:1`; all older direct-message approval containers reject. `provisioningAuthorityIdentity` is rederived from and equals the trusted user-approval message identity, never a repository object or circular approval reference. The campaign request embeds the complete verified `Wave0aBoundControlAuthority`, exact lifecycle-approval `ApprovalIdentity`, exact completed acceptance `FileIdentity`, acceptance-derived `lifecycleExpiresAt`, and one `attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt`; it rejects an `expiresAt` key. A generic campaign `expiresAt` key remains rejected. Only `admitBeginAtomically` compares the clock after reopening the held lifecycle request, approval, claim journal, terminal-seal absence, and acceptance: it requires `approvedAt <= recordedAt`, finalizes/reopens all dependent bytes and the semantic deadline-fence receipt, then requires `recordedAt <= commitFenceNow < attemptStartBefore <= lifecycleExpiresAt` on one ephemeral second sample immediately before native publication. `commitFenceNow` is never serialized or reconstructed after a crash. The combined READY record rejects request/file/hash/value drift, authority/lifecycle approval/lifecycle acceptance crossing, a changed worktree-registry fence, a new root that is no longer absent, an existing root/head/predecessor that no longer verifies, any active or unresolved predecessor attempt, roster/DAG/contract drift, or reuse outside the one bound attempt. No destructive quarantine validator accepts `OrderedMessageObservation` or any manual-capture exemption.

Quarantine approval first create-new writes and reopens a canonical request that embeds the exact no-follow `preflightIdentity`, `preflightSha256`, damaged-tree/root/index/recovery tuple, and mutation scope. With `Q=SHA-256(canonical request bytes)`, attempt-tree quarantine requires the entire prompt/user body `WAVE0A-ATTEMPT-TREE-QUARANTINE-V2 を承認 requestSha256=Q`; campaign-publication quarantine requires `WAVE0A-CAMPAIGN-PUBLICATION-QUARANTINE-V2 を承認 requestSha256=Q`. Each v2 approval embeds that request and identity, repeats the exact preflight identity, carries the provider-backed three-message transcript and `maxUses:1`, and is consumed only after the live preflight and request are re-opened byte-identically. Tests reject source/role/thread/message/order crossing, assistant self-approval, prefix/suffix, request/preflight/hash/value crossing, a transcript copied from either other quarantine scope, any prior `Q`, second use, or a valid approval whose preflight no longer matches live damage. A Wave approval, lifecycle approval, scalar user observation, or legacy manual-capture object can never authorize destructive quarantine.

The semantic producer boundary is closed, not duck-typed: Task 1C alone produces archive preflight; Task 5B produces protected-clone/success-topology/recovery-topology/PR-mergeability/main-integration-reconciliation/terminal-settlement/PR/ref observations; Tasks 4A/4B produce run-set snapshots, run discovery, exact-CI, and partial-run records; Task 6C produces local-gate evidence; Task 6D produces generated-path, deletion-plan, final-cleanup, and cleanup-progress evidence; Task 6F produces the campaign-execution approval request, schema v3 READY approval, event proposals, independent-review request/attachment derivations, failure/candidate-preservation manifests, exact trigger boundaries, and deterministic merge-commit plans; Task 6B produces typed operation inspection; and Task 6G produces mutation request/intent/claim/process-result/termination-proof/receipt plus merge-preparation and all other mutation observations including branch deletion. No Wave 0A producer emits a deferred capability approval, disposition, or `NOT_APPLICABLE` event. `Wave0aMutationSummary` is a separate staging-only projection with its own exact `1_048_576`-byte cap: it is never an `AttachmentPayload`, `EvidenceRef`, `TransactionFilePlan`, campaign-index member, handoff attachment, operation pre/postcondition, or attempt-manifest member, and no campaign publication command accepts its path as evidence. A later builder may accept `--operation-summary` only to reopen the summary's authenticated campaign intent/receipt/postconditions and must emit those durable locators, never the summary path or bytes. The campaign CLI accepts a source only after the owning producer's `verify-existing` mode and the campaign pure semantic validator independently agree.

`AttachmentByteCapBySchema` is the sole exact `schemaVersion -> canonical serialized byte cap` authority for the 42 Wave 0A `AttachmentPayload` discriminants. `CampaignAuthority` has `MAX_CAMPAIGN_AUTHORITY_BYTES=1_048_576`; `AttemptManifest` has `MAX_ATTEMPT_MANIFEST_BYTES=4_194_304`; protected-clone/local-gate and `root-materialization-plan/v1` are `16_777_216`; deletion-plan is `134_217_728`; run-set/partial-run/operation records are `1_048_576`; cleanup-progress and worktree-progress are `4_096`. Approval, quarantine, checkpoint proposal, transaction/marker/lock/reservation, event proposal, handoff, mutation summary, root-fast-forward progress, root-handoff plan/publication-result, controller-release request/companion-result/envelope/activation, controller-child ticket, trigger/recovery/bootstrap/stage-stop/inspection records each have the separately declared `1_048_576` producer/consumer cap. Root materialization additionally enforces at most 16,384 actions, depth 256, 67,108,864 path bytes, 1,073,741,824 bytes per file, 17,179,869,184 aggregate blob bytes, sixteen 1,024-action chunks, and eighteen progress records. Candidate raw bundle/patch/log files are at most `16_777_216` each. Every remaining scalar, aggregate, serialized, decoded/encoded, and process-output limit has producer/consumer `N-1/N/N+1` tests before parse, copy, publication, or execution. The deferred product/UAT/final-attestation identifiers have no Wave 0A cap map or parser and are rejected as unknown.

Task 6A exports one literal valid fixture and validator per Wave 0A producer schema; every later producer policy/test imports that authority rather than retyping it. Shared fixtures cover archive preflight, run discovery, exact CI, every Task 5B topology/timeline attachment, local gates, generated inventory/cleanup, and every in-scope Task 6F/6G record. Producer and campaign tests canonical-render the same fixture and require byte equality. A same-`schemaVersion` object with different keys is a hard failure. Candidate preservation tests independently reopen and validate the three raw bundle/patch/log members; no product package, VSIX, UAT archive, closure attempt, or final-attestation fixture is created in Wave 0A.
Run evidence has a closed four-workflow cardinality. `RunDiscoveryAttachment.selectedRuns` contains exactly the four literal workflow keys; each value's workflow path/key, event, head SHA, ref, title, and dispatch nonce must equal its request and trigger boundary. `ExactHeadCiAttachment.runs` contains those same four runs in workflow-contract order, with every `run.event` equal to the attachment's top-level `event`; PR mode has exactly 12 required successful jobs and no skipped job, while dispatch mode has exactly 11 successful required jobs plus the sole `Extension source metrics` skip. The integer `requiredJobCount` is a checked consequence, not an independent assertion. Tests reject 3/5 runs, mixed event/head/ref/title/nonce, duplicate workflow/run/job IDs, reordered workflows, and any top-level/member crossing.

The tool bundle is not self-declared. `wave0a-tool-bundle.json` and an independent literal path set in `wave0aMutationPolicy.mjs` must contain the same ordinal entrypoint/module/static-asset list; tests parse every static local import, reject dynamic/local resolution and any import outside that set, reject an unused or missing member, and require the PowerShell bootstrap/helper plus every runtime `.mjs`/`.json` dependency used in Tasks 7/8. Exact resource limits are `MAX_TOOL_BUNDLE_MEMBERS=128`, `MAX_TOOL_BUNDLE_MEMBER_BYTES=4_194_304`, and `MAX_TOOL_BUNDLE_TOTAL_BYTES=67_108_864`; `memberCount === modules.length`, `totalBytes` is the canonical decimal sum of those module byte sizes, every entrypoint occurs exactly once in `modules`, and module repository paths are ordinal-sorted and unique. Host launcher, bootstrap, and contract identities are separate from `memberCount/totalBytes`; their existing 1 MiB individual caps apply before parse/materialization. At handoff creation, the producer resolves each path at candidate `H`, requires every `RepoObjectIdentity.containingCommitSha == H`, calls authenticated fixed `git cat-file -s OID` before opening a blob stream, rejects count/per-member/aggregate overflow before materialization, then hashes a stream bounded to the declared size. The aggregate is SHA-256 over canonical ordinal `(repositoryPath,blobOid,byteSize,blobSha256)` tuples. `ToolBundleManifest.hostLauncher` is the separately stage-minus-one-authenticated `run-wave0a-host.ps1` identity and `bootstrap` is the self-contained no-import `wave0a-bootstrap.ps1` identity; neither is inferred from the working tree. Bundle materialization repeats `cat-file -s`, count and running-total checks before each blob, writes absolute authenticated Git `cat-file blob OID` bytes into a fresh contained no-replace tree without buffering past the member cap, then reopens and rehashes every file and executes only absolute entrypoints from that tree. Count 127/128/129, member bytes and aggregate bytes at `N-1/N/N+1`, declared/observed size crossing, truncation/growth, duplicate/unsorted members, entrypoint nonmembership, and producer/rehydrator cap disagreement are RED. The control-plane host imports only authenticated bundle code/static assets; after that host starts, candidate `H` project, test, package, and dependency-policy files may be read only by the closed Task 6C local-gate subprocess argv, under pre/post `H/tree/status` identity checks. Those candidate inputs are never imports or executable control-plane assets. Tests contrast an allowed enumerated local-gate read with a rejected bundle import/dynamic resolution of the same path.

Candidate preservation is binary-aware. The bundle/patch/log bytes are copied as ordinary immutable files named by the three `CandidateBinaryRef` values; they are not falsely parsed as JSON schemas. Before publication, run fixed-array `git bundle verify` and `git apply --check --binary` in a throwaway contained checkout, bind exact `B/H/tree`, hash the raw bytes, and ensure the diagnostic log contains only fixed field names, numeric outcomes, and hashes. Wave 0A has no product package, VSIX installation, UAT archive, or final-attestation producer; the opaque future identifiers cannot be satisfied by candidate-preservation bytes.

`CampaignIndexEntry.previousEntrySha256` is `null` only for sequence 1 and is a required lowercase SHA-256 for every later sequence. Sequence/path/kind must advance by exactly one, and `IndexHead.path` must equal the path derived from its sequence and kind. Manifest artifact/locator sets and other explicitly set-valued arrays are ordinal-sorted, duplicate-free, nonempty where their operation requires content, and bounded by the declared campaign limits. `QuarantineRecord.inventory` is scalar/digest-only and is cross-checked solely against the `damaged-tree-v1` stream; removed per-file identity arrays are invalid unknown keys. `HandoffRehydration.operationProgress` and `FAILED.mutationRecords` use the closed state/operation sequence; `Wave0aMutationRequest.evidence`, `Wave0aMutationIntent.preconditionEvidence`, and matching receipt postconditions use the static mutation-contract label order. `TransactionDescriptor.members` and `TransactionReceipt.publishedMembers` use the closed operation-specific publication order, and the receipt list equals the descriptor's planned ordinal/size/SHA members exactly. Duplicate-free applies only to arrays explicitly declared as sets, locator sequences, labels, or publication members; `CommandObservation.argv`, `Wave0aMutationIntent.argv`, and other fixed command arrays preserve literal contract order and may repeat tokens such as dispatch `-f`. Tests separately accept the required repeated `-f` argv and reject duplicate evidence labels, locators, transaction members, caller-supplied staged/final paths, and descriptor variants whose regenerated path belongs to another scope or owner. Marker, lock, and reservation files contain exactly the canonical JSON schemas above; zero-byte sentinel files are forbidden.

Allowed success transitions are exactly `READY -> LOCAL -> PR_ACTIVE -> MERGED -> POST_MERGE_VERIFIED -> MAIN_ONLY -> VERIFIED`; `FAILED` is terminal from any nonterminal state. Recovery-only profile advances do not add campaign event states: a published pre-merge attempt may move from its exact `LOCAL_PUBLISHED`/`PR_ACTIVE`/`MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED` profile through `PREMERGE_PR_CLOSED`, `PREMERGE_READY_RESTORED`, and the mandatory `PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` profile before terminal `FAILED`. Every Wave 0A runtime object fixes `subject=Wave0aSubject` and `decisionAuthority=Wave0aDecisionAuthority` byte-identically across one attempt. Derive `executionStatus` without operator input: `READY=planned`, `LOCAL|PR_ACTIVE|FAILED=in_progress`, `MERGED|POST_MERGE_VERIFIED|MAIN_ONLY=merged`, and `VERIFIED=validated`. Terminal states accept no later event. Gate/capability subjects, later decision-authority variants, dispositions, and `NOT_APPLICABLE` are unknown inputs, not dormant aliases. Wave 0A requires its exact two omission codes and `observedActivationStatus=inactive` in every state. `nextBoundary` is the exact static next dependency member only; later capability activation and FINAL-VALIDATION closure ordering require a separate approved plan and are not runtime code in this wave.

Operation locators are state-closed and reverified against the campaign `operations/` tree: `PR_ACTIVE` requires exactly publish then create-pull-request; `MERGED` requires prepare-merge-commit, the two-ref integrate-main-exact-lease, then fetch-after-integration; `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED` requires the four dispatch instances in workflow-contract order; `MAIN_ONLY` adds no mutation locator and reopens the integration receipt's branch-absence reconciliation; `VERIFIED` requires cleanup-generated-paths, fast-forward-root, remove-feature-worktree, then delete-local-branch. `FAILED.mutationRecords` is the ordinal operation-instance set actually published before failure and may use `status:'intent_only'` only for the exact unresolved intents named by its latest checkpoint; every other entry is `status:'receipted'`. A completed pre-merge abort additionally requires its normal published prefix followed by exactly `[cleanup-generated-paths]` when no remote residual ever existed, `[delete-remote-branch-abort,cleanup-generated-paths]` for an authenticated absent PR, or `[close-pull-request-abort,delete-remote-branch-abort,cleanup-generated-paths]` for an exact OPEN PR; those recovery-only instances are mutually exclusive with prepare/integrate having an applied main integration, every post-main instance, and every success event. `VERIFIED` and every other success event forbid intent-only and abort locators. A receipted locator whose receipt is not `applied`, whose intent/request/contract/executable/environment/repository/file-argument/current-event binding differs, or whose postcondition evidence drifts cannot satisfy a success state. Task 6A owns and exports the pure immutable `Wave0aOperationEvidenceContract`: exactly all 15 instance IDs plus every closed mode variant, each with ordered nonempty pre/post `{label,schemaVersion}` tuples. Task 6B reserve/publish and Task 6F builders consume that export before Task 6G exists. Task 6G later derives the instance and evidence projection from `wave0a-mutations.json` and requires canonical byte equality with the Task 6A export, so neither implementation order nor spelling drift creates a second authority.

`HandoffRehydration` is also a closed state machine, not a bag of optional fields. `LOCAL_PRE_PUBLISH -> LOCAL_PUBLISHED -> PR_ACTIVE`; `PR_ACTIVE -> MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED -> MERGED_PRE_FETCH -> MERGED` when GitHub PR metadata is already terminal after integration, or `PR_ACTIVE -> MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED -> MAIN_INTEGRATED_PR_PENDING -> MERGED` when it lags and the fetch intent durably binds a later terminal settlement; `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED -> MAIN_ONLY` by a read-only event append that reopens the two-ref integration evidence; and `MAIN_ONLY -> GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED -> ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED -> FEATURE_WORKTREE_REMOVED -> VERIFIED` are the normal within-event profile advances. The recovery suffix is `LOCAL_PRE_PUBLISH -> PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` when no remote residual ever existed, `LOCAL_PUBLISHED -> PREMERGE_READY_RESTORED -> PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` after exact ref deletion with a proven absent PR, or `[PR_ACTIVE|MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED] -> PREMERGE_PR_CLOSED -> PREMERGE_READY_RESTORED -> PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` for an exact PR; all paths retain the current `LOCAL` or `PR_ACTIVE` event state, require the same verified recovery checkpoint in every successor, and end only in terminal FAILED after the clean profile. `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED|POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_TIMEOUT|POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT` are checkpointed controlled stops and never self-upgrade, repoll, retry the push, or enter ordinary cleanup without separate approval. A pending handoff never self-upgrades: Task 5B emits a terminal settlement and separately emits a stable `MERGED_PRE_FETCH` topology; the unique fetch request supplies both as authenticated aggregate-precondition sources, and Task 6B publishes them before the intent commit point. The applied fetch receipt is the only authority for the direct pending-to-`MERGED` successor. The next successful event resets the profile to that event's same-named base profile. The cross-named final profile in each normal chain is explicitly the topology precondition for appending that next event, not the next event itself. `pullRequestNumber` is forbidden in the first two LOCAL profiles, required from `LOCAL/PR_ACTIVE`, and retained through a PR-bearing abort; `mergeSha` is forbidden until an applied deterministic-object preparation establishes `MERGE_COMMIT_PREPARED`, and then must name the same `M` through either later normal profiles or the abort suffix without authorizing integration. `operationProgress` must equal one exact path prefix accepted by the canonical `Wave0aOperationExecutionDag` for the authenticated `(state,resumeProfile,outcome)` and branch-entry guard; the serialization roster proves only membership and uniqueness. No DAG path may duplicate or skip a node, cross a mode, or contain more than its final locator as `intent_only`. That path may additionally end in exactly one receipted normal operation whose verified outcome is `not_applied`; it does not advance the profile and is legal only when the same checkpointed flow either proceeds immediately to its matching remote-recovery operation or freshly proves no remote residual, executes the mandatory `pre_merge_abort_cleanup`, reaches `PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED`, and only then terminal-seals `FAILED/not_required_pre_merge` without a remote-abort intent. `ambiguous`, `contradictory`, or `applied` at that exception position authorizes neither branch. `resumeCheckpoint` is the general root-relative locator for a checkpoint-backed successor: it is forbidden when no checkpoint caused that successor and required for all three abort profiles, both settlement stops, `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT`, or mutation reconciliation. When the final locator is `intent_only`, that checkpoint must have `failureCode:'mutation_reconciliation_required'` and bind the exact intent/event/profile; no other checkpoint authorizes reconciliation. A receipted prefix may carry only the typed non-mutation/manual-decision checkpoint that caused its stop; the no-receipt drift arm instead carries its exact checkpoint-owned reconciliation/topology pair. An owner crossing among event, operation, and controlled-stop topology is forbidden.
