From `$verifiedPostMergeHandoff`, materialize and reverify the durable `integrate-main-exact-lease` summary and its `main-integration-reconciliation/v1` postcondition. Require the applied receipt, packet digest for the real `B -> M` main command and `H -> absent` feature command, exact `main=M/feature=absent`, the same terminal `MERGED/mergeCommitOid=M` settlement already consumed by the `MERGED` event, and the applied `fetch-after-integration` receipt that fixed local `origin/main=M`. Set `$mainOnlyHandoffResult=Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'main-only-handoff-result.txt'` and `$verifiedMainOnlyHandoff=Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'verified-main-only-handoff.json'`; run `create-handoff --expected-state MAIN_ONLY --result $mainOnlyHandoffResult @externalToolArgv`, then `verify-handoff --result $mainOnlyHandoffResult @externalToolArgv --output $verifiedMainOnlyHandoff`. - [ ] **Step 8: Re-audit the destructive boundary, fast-forward root, and remove exact local recovery state**

Immediately before the remaining destructive local operations, run a fresh `GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` topology assessment into `$postMainStagingRoot\generated-clean-pre-local-cleanup.json` with live/origin `$merged`, root `$base`, protected baseline, exact cleanup evidence, and exact active worktree/branch/head. Any mismatch follows FAILED without attempting removal.

Resolve and canonicalize the literal root/target paths with the Task 5 canonicalizer. Every staging root is a newly created non-reparse directory outside the feature worktree, root worktree, protected clone, and campaign; containment or identity overlap rejects before host launch. The authenticated tool bundle lives under `$postMainStagingRoot` and remains the sole executable source for that one phase.

The first post-cleanup process may perform only `fast_forward_root` from `$verifiedGeneratedCleanHandoff` to literal `$merged`, with ordered caller evidence `generated-cleanup=$generatedCleanupPath` and `archive-preflight-final=$archivePreflightFinalPath`. The caller never supplies a materialization plan. Task 6G derives the exact `B -> M` no-follow `root-materialization-plan/v1`, publishes it internally as the final aggregate precondition (`0004` for success, `0005` for checkpoint-backed failure), and binds the same `FeatureAndRootWorktreeRegistryFence{registrationSet:'feature_and_root'}` into the materialization plan, `RootFastForwardPlan`, request, and every progress record. The held fence requires exactly root `HEAD -> refs/heads/main` at `B` with target `M` and linked feature `HEAD -> refs/heads/$branch` at `H/H`. The native supervisor holds the common-Git `worktrees` registry/admin directories, root/admin `HEAD`, linked-worktree `.git`, and admin `gitdir` no-follow handles from final pre-spawn validation through result receipt; any add/move/remove/prune registration change, either HEAD retarget, handle replacement, or identity drift rejects.

The closed program is exactly: (1) `git -c core.hooksPath=NUL update-ref --no-deref --stdin`, whose policy-generated fixed UTF-8/LF transaction verifies direct `HEAD -> refs/heads/main` and CAS-updates only `main B -> M`; (2) the authenticated native helper `materialize-root-exact --intent CAMPAIGN_INTENT --plan CAMPAIGN_PLAN --progress-root CAMPAIGN_PROGRESS --payload-root FRESH_PAYLOAD_DIRECTORY --output-root FRESH_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`, which reads only the plan-bound blob payload and materializes the tracked root tree via held no-follow handles; then (3) `git -c core.hooksPath=NUL read-tree M`, index only. The last command has no `-m` or `-u`; checkout, reset, clean, and Git worktree materialization remain forbidden. Each plan/progress/receipt reopens the same registry fence and root/index/worktree tree OIDs, and only exact contiguous recovery prefixes are legal.

After the applied receipt, resolve `$durableFinalArchivePreflight` from the campaign-owned intent precondition. Invoke the single supervised `publish-root-handoff` command shown below; that one claim plans the complete `ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED` handoff/index bytes, writes the current-controller release request containing that plan, commits/adopts exactly that planned handoff, writes the durable authority-root companion result and envelope, and finally writes one staging `RootHandoffPublicationResult`. The authenticated handoff bytes switch `bootstrapRepository` to root `M`, while the compact token only authenticates those bytes. Parse and reverify the complete result schema, create/verify the canonical `root_handoff_ready` stop naming its envelope, and exit 42. This is a mandatory phase boundary: the feature-bootstrapped process is forbidden to return success, reserve, or spawn `remove_feature_worktree`, `delete_local_branch`, or the next controller.

A fresh supervisor-selected root generation reopens the durable release quartet and active tree, authenticates root `HEAD=main=M`, parents `[B,H]`, and equal tree, and only then may run `remove_feature_worktree`. Outer, host, operator, Task 6G child, and native helper all use the authenticated root CWD. The request embeds the bootstrap-result path and immutable pre-intent release/tree proof; the actual helper PID/CWD is added only to the claim. Task 6G publishes the immutable `WorktreeRemovalPlan`, and the native helper accepts only the campaign intent/plan/progress root plus a fresh output root. A crash authenticates the exact missing prefix and resumes only the undisposed suffix under the same intent; partial prefix state is expected, while gaps, replacement, reparse, unexpected children, registration/release/CWD drift, or a second disposition are contradictory. Only a fully applied receipt advances to `FEATURE_WORKTREE_REMOVED`, then branch deletion; no Git/GitHub remote operation is respawned.

The operator sequence is literal:

```powershell
$generatedCleanTopologyPath = Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'generated-clean-pre-local-cleanup.json'
& $nodeExecutable (Join-Path $authenticatedToolRoot 'tools\main-consolidation\audit-slice-topology.mjs') assess `
  --snapshot-profile GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED `
  --expected-live-main $merged --expected-origin-main $merged --expected-root-main $base `
  --expected-base $base --expected-merge $merged --merge-preparation $mergePreparationPath `
  --root-worktree $rootWorktree --protected-clone-baseline $protectedCloneBaseline `
  --active-worktree $featureWorktree --active-branch $branch --expected-feature-head $head `
  --pull-request $prNumber --generated-after $generatedAfterAttachment --generated-cleanup $generatedCleanupPath `
  --external-tool-authority $bootstrapResultPath --git-executable $gitExecutable --gh-executable $ghExecutable `
  --output $generatedCleanTopologyPath
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED topology failed' }

$fastForwardSummaryPath = Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'fast-forward-root-summary.json'
$fastForwardOutcome = Invoke-Wave0aOperation -OperationId fast_forward_root `
  -OperationInstanceId fast-forward-root -VerifiedHandoffPath $verifiedGeneratedCleanHandoff `
  -HandoffToken $generatedCleanHandoffToken -TopologyPath $generatedCleanTopologyPath `
  -StagingRoot $postMainStagingRoot `
  -Evidence @("generated-cleanup=$generatedCleanupPath","archive-preflight-final=$archivePreflightFinalPath")
Assert-Wave0aOperationContinuation -Outcome $fastForwardOutcome
if ($fastForwardOutcome.summaryPath -cne $fastForwardSummaryPath) { throw 'root fast-forward summary path mismatch' }
$fastForwardSummary = Read-ClosedMutationSummary -LiteralPath $fastForwardSummaryPath -ExpectedInstance 'fast-forward-root'
$durableFinalArchivePreflight = Get-UniqueOperationPrecondition -Summary $fastForwardSummary `
  -Label 'archive-preflight-final' -ExpectedSchema 'bob-builtin-analyze/feature-integration-archive-preflight/v1'
$rootFastForwardedTopologyPath = Get-UniqueMutationPostcondition -Summary $fastForwardSummary `
  -ExpectedSchema 'bob-builtin-analyze/slice-topology-evidence/v1'

$rootHandoffPublicationResult = Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'root-fast-forwarded-publication-result.json'
$rootFastForwardReceipt = Get-UniqueOperationReceiptEvidence -Summary $fastForwardSummary
& $nodeExecutable $campaignTool publish-root-handoff `
  --root $campaignRoot --attempt-id $attemptId `
  --source-verified-handoff $verifiedGeneratedCleanHandoff `
  --expected-state MAIN_ONLY --expected-profile ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED `
  --operation-receipt $rootFastForwardReceipt `
  --active-controller-tree $activeControllerTreePath `
  @externalToolArgv --output $rootHandoffPublicationResult
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED handoff publication failed' }
$rootPublication = Read-ClosedRootHandoffPublicationResult -LiteralPath $rootHandoffPublicationResult `
  -ExpectedState MAIN_ONLY -ExpectedProfile ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED
$controllerReleaseRequest = $rootPublication.request.canonicalPath
$rootHandoffResult = $rootPublication.companionResult.canonicalPath
$controllerReleaseEnvelope = $rootPublication.envelope.canonicalPath
$verifiedRootFastForwardedHandoff = Join-Path $postMainStagingRoot 'verified-root-fast-forwarded-handoff.json'
& $nodeExecutable $campaignTool verify-handoff `
  --result $rootHandoffResult @externalToolArgv --output $verifiedRootFastForwardedHandoff
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw 'ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED handoff verification failed' }
$rootFastForwardedProjection = Read-ClosedVerifiedHandoff -LiteralPath $verifiedRootFastForwardedHandoff `
  -ExpectedState MAIN_ONLY -ExpectedProfile ROOT_FAST_FORWARDED
$rootFastForwardedHandoffToken = [string]$rootFastForwardedProjection.handoffToken
Assert-RootHandoffReady -Projection $rootFastForwardedProjection `
  -HandoffResult $rootHandoffResult -RootWorktree $rootWorktree `
  -ExpectedBase $base -ExpectedHead $head -ExpectedMerge $merged
```

## Failure, recovery, and campaign closure

Every started healthy attempt must eventually end in `VERIFIED` or `FAILED`; an operator may not simply abandon it. The explicitly typed pre-merge main-drift stop and three controlled post-integration stops may hold the attempt nonterminal while awaiting separate approval, but no current-plan transition can treat a hold as closure. Execute this exact order:

1. Capture the actual last successful event/state, exact base/head/tree/live/origin/root main, named PR/ref/run observations, every existing operation intent/receipt, failing command outcome hashes, and current/recovery topology through the owning bounded producers. Preserve published bytes.
2. Before recording the first failure that leaves any remote or local residual state, run Task 6F `preserve-candidate`. It creates and verifies an exact `B..H` Git bundle, binary patch, and redacted diagnostic log, then the manifest whose final campaign-relative target paths were derived from the verified handoff/event sequence before creation. The first campaign checkpoint transaction validates those unused targets and copies/revalidates all four byte-identical files; it never rewrites or reserializes the manifest. Every later failure/checkpoint in the same attempt must reopen and reuse that one campaign-owned preservation set, never run `preserve-candidate` again or create a second raw payload. If preservation cannot prove `H/tree`, stop without cleanup or further mutation.
3. Use Task 6F—not manual JSON—to create the failure and `RecoveryCheckpointProposal`; run `checkpoint --expected-state ACTUAL_STATE` with the exact `resumeProfile`, complete cumulative-v2 operation path/digest, latest topology, preservation, failure, PR/ref/run, and any sole unresolved-intent evidence, then `verify-campaign`. Immediately run `create-handoff --result NEW_RESULT` for the same nonterminal state and `verify-handoff --result NEW_RESULT --output NEW_VERIFIED`; parse only that verified output. Every stop or session boundary selects exactly one continuation route. An explicit human/task handoff that does not return phase exit 42 reports the verified `{campaignRoot,handoffPath,handoffToken}` triple. A phase exit 42 reports the canonical `StageStopResult` plus exactly the continuation fixed by its reason: a verified companion `HandoffResult`, a `TerminalSealRecoveryResult`, or for `independent_review_pending` only, the unchanged verified handoff triple plus external review request/attestation paths described by `ReviewResumeContinuation`. It never mixes those reason-bound forms or appends a second generic triple. Only a companion `HandoffResult` or the independent-review held handoff can enter a fresh business invocation; a terminal-seal result has no business continuation and the stop file itself is diagnostic nonauthority. If the process crashes between checkpoint and successor handoff, a later recovery invocation uses the last reported authenticated `Handoff` triple or `HandoffResult`, never both, only for built-in stage 0 plus `authenticate-historical`; authenticated operator mode `recover` records its new durable result and stops. A further fresh invocation runs strict `rehydrate` on that new result before any reconciliation. Stdout-only values, shell/process variables, guessed paths, a stop file as authority, or simultaneous continuation forms are forbidden. Tests enumerate all three reason-bound phase continuations plus the non-42 task-handoff route and prove exact exclusivity.
4. Ordinary pre-merge recovery chooses abort/new-attempt; Wave 0A never amends `H` or repairs the same PR with a new head. Require main live/origin/root exactly `B`, durable preservation/failure/checkpoint, and topology proving no remote residual, exact ref `H` with authenticated absent PR, or ref `H` plus the exact OPEN/unmerged PR. Integrated `M` switches to the post-merge state machine; every other identity remains stopped. Close only the exact PR when present and require `PREMERGE_PR_CLOSED`; then exact-lease delete only ref `H`. If the applied delete re-observes main still `B`, require `PREMERGE_READY_RESTORED` and continue the ordinary abort suffix. If it proves `applied_with_main_drift`, require `PREMERGE_BRANCH_DELETED_MAIN_DRIFT` at `K/B/B`, retain the exact delete receipt/`C_abort`/preservation/checkpoint/companion, and thereafter only reissue `reason:'premerge_main_drift'` with exit 42. That hold cannot run generated cleanup, terminal-seal, retry/replay a mutation, rebaseline, or start a new attempt under this plan. Lease mismatch, disappearance after applied publication, PR drift, or any other ambiguous outcome never falls back. Only restored/no-remote-residual branches create or reopen one immutable `pre_merge_abort_cleanup` plan from campaign-owned generated inventories, execute/reconcile only the `cleanup-generated-paths` same-intent suffix, and require `PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` plus all allowlisted outputs absent. Only then run an ordinary READY-shaped assessment without appending a second READY event and terminal-append `FAILED`: `not_required_pre_merge` when no remote mutation was needed, otherwise `completed_pre_merge_abort` with `[cleanup]`, `[delete,cleanup]`, or `[close,delete,cleanup]` as applicable. Only after that terminal manifest/index reverify may a new request-hash-approved `existing_campaign_new_attempt` bind the exact FAILED head/predecessor, a new unused attempt ID and immutable `H`, skip `init`, and repeat READY/local gates/exact-head CI/independent review in the retained root. Superseding a main-drift hold instead requires a separately captured baseline/disposition approval and a replacement plan; it is not this automatic successor.
5. At `MAIN_INTEGRATED_PR_PENDING`, require live main at distinct `M`, origin/root `B`, applied preparation/exact-lease receipts, parents `[B,H]`, equal trees, the feature ref already absent, and the named PR OPEN; permit exactly one bounded read-only settlement producer call from that non-stop boundary. `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_CLOSED`, `POST_MERGE_PR_SETTLEMENT_TIMEOUT`, and `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT` permit only checkpoint/handoff revalidation and the same canonical exit-42 stop until separate approval; they never repoll or enter fetch/dispatch/cleanup. At `MERGED`, require that PR terminal `MERGED` with `mergeCommitOid=M`, live/origin `M`, and remote heads already main-only. Each dispatch first preserves failure-entry capacity; a typed non-observed/ambiguous receipt enters `main_dispatch_failed/POST_MERGE_DISPATCH_FAILED` after a legal one-to-four prefix. Main run discovery is published once through its receipt-backed transaction; typed exit 20 enters `main_run_discovery_failed/POST_MERGE_RUN_DISCOVERY_FAILED`. CI exit 21 enters `ci_failed/POST_MERGE_CI_FAILED`; exit 20 retries only while capacity admits it, otherwise enters `ci_ambiguous/POST_MERGE_CI_AMBIGUOUS`. Success alone appends `POST_MERGE_VERIFIED`, which advances directly to `MAIN_ONLY` by reopening the integration reconciliation and fresh main-only topology. Each of the four failure profiles likewise begins directly with the four local cleanup successors through `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_LOCAL_MAIN_ONLY`; no normal or failure remote-delete/fetch operation exists after integration. Never reset/force-push main or claim an in-attempt product rollback.
6. At normal `MAIN_ONLY` and every post-main failure-cleanup profile, remote mutation is disabled. The four local operations remain ordered: generated cleanup, root fast-forward, worktree removal, branch deletion. The first three are journaled same-intent suffix programs: generated cleanup resumes chunks; root fast-forward resumes only the exact contiguous progress prefix across main-ref CAS, bounded no-follow materialization chunks, and final index-only verification under the same `feature_and_root` registry fence; and worktree removal resumes only the exact undisposed contiguous delete suffix. Branch deletion never respawns: an exact absent branch is reconciled read-only against its intent/postcondition, while an unreceipted request reacquires the fresh `root_only` fence before its one exact CAS. Already applied prefixes are never repeated; a progress/worktree gap or any unmatched state is contradictory and checkpointed.
7. After applicable recovery, Task 6F creates literal `FAILED` from the newest verified handoff. Pre-merge context alone carries typed PR/ref observations and may use `not_completed` only where the pre-merge outcome union explicitly permits a partial cleanup checkpoint; `PREMERGE_BRANCH_DELETED_MAIN_DRIFT` is excluded from every terminal failure proposal. After `M` integration, the four post-main cleanup-entry failures remain nonterminal until the four-operation local-cleanup suffix completes; `rollbackOutcome=not_completed` is forbidden. Their completed context contains the `MERGED` event's exact integration settlement, the `integrate-main-exact-lease` reconciliation proving feature absence, and final `delete-local-branch` topology, and forbids generic PR/ref observations. The pre-merge drift stop and three controlled post-integration stops are not members of the four-way failure union, cannot use either cleanup suffix, and cannot produce `FAILED` or any success event without a separately approved new disposition and replacement plan. The diagnostic union is exact: CI has run-discovery plus one matching partial, dispatch has only its operation postcondition, and discovery failure has only its typed failure attachment. `completed_pre_merge_abort` requires its exact cleanup/remote-abort tuple and `PREMERGE_GENERATED_PATHS_CLEANED` and forbids the drift profile and post-main locators. `completed_post_merge_cleanup` requires event state `MERGED`, one of the four matching initial profiles, exact four-operation tuple `[cleanup-generated-paths,fast-forward-root,remove-feature-worktree,delete-local-branch]`, `POST_MERGE_FAILURE_LOCAL_MAIN_ONLY`, no generated residue/ref/branch/worktree, and `revert_required/M`. Invoke terminal `append` once, then `verify-attempt` and `verify-campaign`.
8. Candidate source/head/tree drift after `READY` is checkpointed and sealed `FAILED`; Step 4 remote/generated cleanup completes first wherever applicable. A new attempt is reachable only through `existing_campaign_new_attempt`: it binds the retained root/current FAILED head, uses a new ID and immutable candidate `H`, never reinitializes the campaign, and reruns READY/archive/topology, every local gate, causally new exact-head CI, and only then independent review. No old result carries forward, and an aborted PR is never reopened or updated.
9. Main-integration reconciliation ambiguity uses Task 5B's exact 600,000 ms / 5,000 ms / 120-poll contract. All process outcomes and runner crashes reconcile the named PR/live main without another push. Timeout or contradictory identity is checkpointed and handed off; the one valid applied-then-`K` sequence instead enters `POST_INTEGRATION_MAIN_DRIFT` and thereafter only reissues its controlled stop.
10. Once remote main-only is proven and a failed post-merge attempt is sealed, any product revert is a separate explicitly user-approved campaign/branch/PR with its own gates and evidence. This attempt never starts one.
11. Campaign authority, a receipt-verified/earlier index entry, or unrelated evidence damage remains an unconditional hard stop. Attempt-local incomplete/orphan publication uses separately approved attempt-tree `quarantine`. Claim-bound campaign-publication damage uses owner-death proof and later exact approval, preserves every raw byte, creates the typed root fence and all seven recovery controls before CAS, removes only the approved descending index prefix while the old lock remains, CAS-removes that lock, installs a recovery-bound lock and the one `attempt_quarantined` replacement/receipt, then removes recovery lock and root fence last. The authenticated CAS authority derives every target; attempt ID/phase/path are never CLI inputs. Neither recovery is automatic, and preserved orphan/partial bytes remain expected evidence.
12. Archive mismatch, protected-clone aggregate drift, unexpected ref/PR/worktree, incomplete pagination, ambiguous run discovery, missing/skipped required job, noncanonical evidence, or failed checkpoint/handoff verification is always fail-closed.

## Mandatory downstream continuation and final Program completion

After Wave 0A, this Program must continue through the normative roadmap rather than terminate at plan generation. `programAtomicSlices` contains exactly 20 mandatory downstream mutation slices: Wave 0B one; Workflow B four; Workflow C five; Processing three plus three plus three; and `FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` one. The 17 `selected` capability rows are therefore not the whole catalog. Gate P is a required repository-non-mutating completion observation after P7 and is not a mutation slice. The optional zero-or-one FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE is derived solely from the closed finalValidationPolicy.closure descriptor, outside the mandatory catalog. The required sequence is exactly:

1. `WAVE-0B-SELECTION-LEDGER`: deterministically materialize and independently review the full source universe, four-disposition selection ledger, generated Markdown, validators, recovery/status contract, and all three versioned downstream plan-authoring/implementation/workspace-disposition protocol families; unclassified or multiply owned source items must be zero, and replay/interrupted-workspace recovery tests must pass.
2. `WORKFLOW-B-GATE-P`: integrate P4, P5, P6 shadow, and P7 as four separate `VERIFIED` mutation slices, then record the required non-mutating Gate P exact-main completion observation before admitting Workflow C.
3. `WORKFLOW-C-SAFE-PREFIX`: integrate Gate R inventory/active manifest, R1, R2, Contribution lifecycle, and Contribution evidence as five separate `VERIFIED` slices while public/product runtime reachability remains zero.
4. `PROCESSING-FOUNDATION`: integrate T13, T14, and T15 separately while preserving current OOXML snapshot/parser/GUI contracts.
5. `PROCESSING-CONTROL`: integrate T16, T17 deadline, and T17 path separately with required Linux/Windows process/path evidence.
6. `PROCESSING-INTEGRITY`: integrate T18 report, CCR handoff, and Bazaar handoff separately, permitting only complete validated atomic handoffs.
7. `FINAL-VALIDATION`: first integrate the ordinary PR-bearing `FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL` slice and require it `VERIFIED`; only then freeze that exact merged main/tree/payload manifest as product main. On that unchanged product identity run the ordered non-mutating phases `aggregate local/hosted gates -> fresh three-VSIX build/hash -> same-artifact real-machine UAT -> read-only final topology audit` and record them in one external attestation. Only if repository publication is required, run at most one later docs/evidence-only `FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE` atomic slice and prove its product payload byte-identical; otherwise the external attestation marks the boundary `VERIFIED` at the product main.

For every PR-bearing atomic slice, admission uses one closed derived descriptor: an exact mandatory catalog row, or the sole optional descriptor from FINAL-VALIDATION.finalValidationPolicy.closure. Its exact immediate predecessor terminal VERIFIED identity and exact main are mandatory; optional closure additionally binds the all-twenty VERIFIED history, control terminal identity, successful ordered-phase attestation, exact fixed product main/tree/payload, and no prior different closure. Caller-supplied IDs or a merely completed boundary label are insufficient. Before committing its detailed plan, the exact current main/tree/topology, complete derived descriptor and initial admission identity/evidence, predecessor record, one planned plan path, one planned branch/worktree name/path, and the derived admin/registration paths' expected-absence state must have the `PROGRAM-SLICE-PLAN-AUTHORING-V1` request-hash approval defined above; immediately after creation, the actual branch/worktree/admin identities must be captured and authenticated as its result. Before any product/source mutation, that committed plan's exact commit/blob/SHA-256/base and the same authenticated workspace must have the later `PROGRAM-SLICE-IMPLEMENTATION-V1` approval; no second workspace is created. Before any remote mutation, a distinct exact-candidate campaign request-hash approval is mandatory. Each such slice must pass local gates, exact PR-head CI, independent Critical 0 / Important 0 review, exact merge/settlement, exact-main CI, and bounded cleanup to main-only. An interrupted authoring/implementation workspace remains preserved until a separate `PROGRAM-SLICE-WORKSPACE-DISPOSITION-V1` request-hash approval chooses retain or exact dispose; disposal first verifies external bundle/patch/status/staged/untracked preservation, then journals exact worktree removal and exact-lease local-ref deletion, and recovery continues only that same legal prefix. It cannot authorize remote/campaign mutation or successor skip. The non-mutating `FINAL-VALIDATION` phases instead remain on one fixed product main and create no PR slice; only the optional single closure publication uses the three mutation approvals. Any drift or failed gate stops that slice or validation phase and all successors; a static disposition cannot be rewritten to make execution green.

Mandatory Program completion requires Wave 0A and all exact 20 catalog rows, including `FINAL-VALIDATION-CONTROL`, to have their terminal `VERIFIED` evidence in predecessor order, the required non-mutating Gate P completion observation, all 17 `selected` capability rows externally evidenced as `validated`, all `conditional` rows remaining unintegrated conditional or having a separate validated post-mandatory campaign, and every `rejected_current_snapshot` implementation and superseded archive/duplicate authority absent from main while the selected/current-main replacement authority remains intact. Exact fixed-product-main local/hosted/UAT gates must be green and the closure attestation durable. With no closure slice, that attestation names the unchanged product main as final verified main. With `FINAL-VALIDATION-CLOSURE`, that sole optional slice must itself be terminal VERIFIED under its bound admission identity; the attestation separately names product main and closure main and proves exact product payload identity across them. In either arm, remote heads must be exactly `['main']`, open PRs 0, local branches exactly `['main']`, registered worktrees exactly the root, local-only `refs/archive/**` 0, `main == origin/main == live remote main`, and the protected nested clone must retain its approved no-follow identity/bytes.
